The unnormalized statement needs no activation frequency.
s5.wave-vector-bounds.TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_labelWaveV: Let $X$ be the flow of a jointly $C^2$ unit-periodic velocity on an interval containing $0$ and $t_0$. Suppose both forward and inverse deformation norms are at most $\mathsf D>0$, and put $\kappa(t,a)=DX_{t,0}(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. The formal statement bounds $|\kappa|$ between $|k_*|/\mathsf D$ and $\mathsf D|k_*|$. It does not mention $\lambda$ or the activation normalization. Substituting $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$ and combining these comparisons gives all four bounds in (5.3). In the normalized statement, $\lambda>0$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$ and $\mathsf D\ge1$ are required. The unnormalized statement needs no activation frequency.

s5.profile-width.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width: The formal expression defines $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ using a real exponent. For the parent hypothesis $\lambda\ge1$, it has its ordinary meaning $h=1/\sqrt\lambda$ and gives $0<h\le1$, exactly the range required for the phase profiles. The definition is also a function of arbitrary real $\lambda$; analytic conclusions in this section use it only in the positive-frequency range and do not infer profile properties from the definition alone.

s5.origin-normalization.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin: On $[t_0,T]$, let $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$ and let $\mathbf a$ be a nonzero transverse solution of $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$. Put $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $b$ at the origin must satisfy $|b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ there. The formal condition also requires $\gamma(t)\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$, with $\lambda\ge1$ supplied by the parent. It therefore gives $0<\gamma\le1$ but does not assert $\max\gamma=1$. The formal statement also permits a smaller nonzero seed.

s5.seed-nonzero.TorusEuler.linearODE_ne_zero_of_mem: Let $J$ be an interval in $\mathbb R$, let $A(t)$ be a continuous family of bounded linear maps on a real normed space, and let $x$ solve $x_t=A(t)x$ at every $t\in J$, with derivatives taken within $J$. If $x(t_0)\ne0$ at one $t_0\in J$, the formal statement proves $x(t)\ne0$ for every $t\in J$. Applied to the central amplitude equation, this is the paper’s nonvanishing argument. The continuous coefficient and genuine solution hypotheses are essential; a nonzero value of an arbitrary function would not suffice.

s5.weight-and-coupling.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight: Given a frequency $\lambda$ and central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$, define $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. The quotation defines both $\gamma$ and $\nu$. This expression defines only $\gamma$ and gives no formula for $\nu$.
s5.weight-and-coupling.TorusEuler.hasDerivWithinAt_movingFrame: For a trace-free matrix $M$ and nonzero perpendicular vectors $\kappa,\mathbf a$ solving $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, set $e_1=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $e_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $e_3=e_1\times e_2$. The formal statement proves the moving-frame differential equations using $\nu=e_1\cdot Me_2$. This is the paper’s coupling at the origin. It does not define the amplitude weight $\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. A separate coefficient $e_1\cdot Me_3$ in that frame calculation has no such meaning. Thus the declaration contains the coupling as part of a different differential statement, not both displayed definitions.

s5.projected-activation.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn: For supplied $M(t,a)$, $\kappa(t,a)$ and central amplitude $c(t)$ on $[t_0,T]$, the formal seed data require $\mathbf a(t,0)=c(t)$, $\mathbf a(t_0,a)=(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})c(t_0)$, $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$ and $\kappa\cdot\mathbf a=0$. Thus the quoted projection is exactly a defining condition. These data also include nearby-label amplitude and positive-coupling estimates; they are not merely a record of initial data. The declaration does not assert existence of an object satisfying those conditions.
s5.projected-activation.TorusEuler.oscillatoryTransverseProjecti: This defines $I-P_\kappa$, the projection used in the displayed initial condition. It does not assert that a seed starts from that value. At $\kappa=0$ the formal expression is the identity because division by zero is zero. The paper excludes that case.
s5.projected-activation.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed: The projection uses $P_\kappa=(\kappa\otimes\kappa)/|\kappa|^2$. At zero covector the quotient is defined as zero. The smooth-flow and nonzero-carrier assumptions exclude that case in this application.

s5.seed-even.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.eve: On $[t_0,T]$, $t_0\le T$, assume $M(t,a)$ and $\kappa(t,a)$ are continuous in time for each label, even in $a$, and $\kappa$ never vanishes. Let $\mathbf a$ solve $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$ with projected initial data $(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})c(t_0)$. The formal statement proves $\mathbf a(t,-a)=\mathbf a(t,a)$ throughout the active interval. Evenness of the coefficients and initial data permits uniqueness of the same linear equation at $a$ and $-a$. This is the parity assertion for the paper’s localized seed.

s5.radial-envelope.TorusEuler.radialEnvelope: The formal envelope is $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$, where one particular smooth function $\chi$ equals one for arguments at most one and zero for arguments at least two, with values in $[0,1]$. For $\ell_*>0$, the resulting field is even, equals one on $|a|\le\ell_*$ and vanishes for $|a|\ge2\ell_*$. These are the properties prescribed in §5.1; the formalization fixes this cutoff rather than quantifying over every possible choice. The formula is also defined at $\ell_*=0$: division by zero is zero, giving $g\equiv1$.

s5.envelope-plateau.TorusEuler.radialEnvelope_eq_one: For the fixed radial cutoff $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$, assume $\ell_*>0$ and $|a|\le\ell_*$. Then $g(a)=1$. The positivity assumption makes $|a|/\ell_*\le1$, where the chosen smooth cutoff is exactly one. This is the plateau property required in §5.1 and used when computing the central gradient. The assertion is only about the spatial envelope in parent labels. It does not assert that the time cutoff is one, or by itself prove that the physical leading wave is active. Other admissible radial cutoffs are not quantified over.

s5.leading-profile.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.lea: The paper writes $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$ for any fixed admissible envelope. The formal statement proves the identity for the chosen radial envelope only, one admissible choice.
s5.leading-profile.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading: The paper defines $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$ after fixing an admissible cutoff. The formal definition uses one particular radial envelope, so the formula is retained for that choice rather than quantified over all admissible cutoffs.

s5.switched-profile.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen: On the centered label cell the formal construction evaluates its leading profile as $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$. The seed data supply the local amplitude and phase profile, while the supplied cutoff multiplies the resulting field in time. The lemma is this local evaluation identity. Smooth switching and its derivative bounds are proved elsewhere.

s5.central-transverse-assumptions.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_see: On $[t_0,T]$, assume nonzero perpendicular $\kappa,c$ with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $c_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mc$. The formal stability hypothesis quantifies over every transverse homogeneous solution $b$: $|b(t)|/|c(t)|\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/|c(t')|$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For $\lambda>0$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|c|$, the constant frequency factor cancels, giving exactly the first inequality in (5.5). The second is imposed as $\kappa\cdot Mc\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||c|$, equivalent to $\nu\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ because both vectors are nonzero. These are hypotheses. The seed construction uses them rather than proving central stability.
s5.central-transverse-assumptions.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.CenterWave: On $[t_0,T]$, assume nonzero perpendicular $\kappa,c$ with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $c_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mc$. The formal stability hypothesis quantifies over every transverse homogeneous solution $b$: $|b(t)|/|c(t)|\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/|c(t')|$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For $\lambda>0$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|c|$, the constant frequency factor cancels, giving exactly the first inequality in (5.5). The second is imposed as $\kappa\cdot Mc\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||c|$, equivalent to $\nu\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ because both vectors are nonzero. These are hypotheses. The seed construction uses them rather than proving central stability.

s5.near-center-size.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn: The formal localized-seed data include, for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ and $|a|\le2\ell_*$, $|\mathbf a(t,0)|/2\le|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, as well as $|\mathbf a(t,a)-\mathbf a(t,0)|\le C|a||\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling. The upper inequality is exactly the paper’s factor-two bound. Because this declaration specifies the data a localized seed must carry, it assumes these estimates as part of those data. The existence theorem is what constructs a seed satisfying them.

s5.leading-velocity-size.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.wei: For a localized seed, let $\lambda\ge1$, $\ell_*>0$, $D\ge1$, $0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$ and $\mathbf a(t,0)\ne0$ at a time in $[t_0,T]$. On $|a|\le2\ell_*$ assume $\lambda\le D^2|\kappa(t,a)|$ and $\|M(t,a)\|\le D$. With $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, and the fixed radial envelope and phase profile, the formal statement proves $|\widetilde\chi g\mathbf aF_h|/\gamma\le\lambda^{-5/4}$. It also bounds $\lambda$ times the corresponding pressure divided by $\gamma$ by $4D^3\lambda^{-5/4}$. The paper’s unweighted velocity estimate additionally uses $\gamma\le1$; that upper bound is not assumed here.

s5.parent-smallness.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The residual bound is a uniform supremum bound over time and the unit torus. It is assumed, not deduced from the Fourier support.
s5.parent-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent: The residual bound is a uniform supremum bound over time and the unit torus. It is assumed, not deduced from the Fourier support.

s5.envelope-radius.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius: The definition supplies $\ell_*=(\mathsf D^a)^{-1}$ for a nonnegative integer $a$. It does not choose an absolute exponent or prove that one choice works uniformly for all subsequent estimates. That order of choices is asserted by the later numbered results.

s5.envelope-in-cell.TorusEuler.tsupport_radialEnvelope_subse: The conclusion places the closed support in $|a|\le2\ell_*$, with $\ell_*>0$. It does not mention the periodic cell. Using the separate bounds $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-3}$ and $\mathsf D\ge2$ gives $2\ell_*\le1/4<1/2$, which yields the paper’s interior inclusion.

r5-B-uniform-exponents.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6: The paper states a convention for all constants denoted $C$. For the hierarchy estimates, the formal statement chooses a single nonnegative integer exponent after the fixed envelope exponent and before the parent, wave, derivative order, level and depth. This verifies the convention for (5.34)–(5.38). It is not a statement about every other occurrence of $C$ in the paper.
r5-B-uniform-exponents.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1: For the coefficient and composition bounds, the formal statement chooses one integer exponent before the parent, wave and all derivative orders. The composition constants are allowed to depend on the input derivative-bound sequence. This supports the asserted uniformity in Proposition 5.1; it does not make a global assertion about all constants elsewhere.

r5-B-order-and-depth-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6: The formal hierarchy theorem chooses a sequence $C_{n,p}$ before the parent and the terminal depth, and a separate sequence $C_{m,P}$ for the finite sums and remainder. Thus a retained level has an order-and-level constant independent of how far the expansion is continued. This is the indicated dependence for Theorem 5.6; the declaration does not specify the constants of other results.

r5-B-no-order-growth-assumption.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6: The formal statement supplies constants at every derivative order but imposes no quantitative growth rate on that sequence. It therefore makes no analytic or Gevrey regularity assertion and no claim of convergence of an infinite hierarchy at fixed frequency. This concerns the theorem’s hypotheses and conclusion. It is not a separate verification of every later use of constants in the iteration.

p5.1.derivative-weights.TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection: The definition permits arbitrary real scales, although the physical estimates take $\ell_*>0$ and $h>0$. Derivative indices are ordered only to represent each multi-index once. The derivative directions are the three operators $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ and the phase operator $h\partial_s$. Thus mixed derivatives acquire exactly the weights $\ell_*^m h^j$ in (D.1). This is the scaling convention behind the finite expansion estimates. It specifies how derivatives are measured and is not itself a bound on a field.
p5.1.derivative-weights.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and time set $I$, the expression sums $\sup_{t\in I,a,s}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j(\tau(t)f)|$ over $|\alpha|+j\le n$, counting each multi-index once. Only label and phase variables are differentiated. Each supremum is implemented as a real supremum of a set that also contains zero; if that set is unbounded above, the expression has default value zero. Thus a finite numerical value alone does not establish boundedness. Analytic estimates separately require or prove boundedness of the derivative sets. With $\tau=\gamma^{-1}$ this gives the weighted norm of Appendix D when $\gamma>0$; division by zero otherwise gives zero. These conventions do not assert any estimate for an unbounded field or a vanishing weight.

p5.1.phase-independent-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteMixedWordNorm_: For a field $c(t,a)$ smooth in $a$, with arbitrary time index set and real normed target, let $f(t,a,s)=c(t,a)$. The formal statement gives exact equality of the mixed norm using directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i},h\partial_s$ and the label norm using $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$. All derivatives containing $\partial_s$ vanish. Thus the common expression is $\sum_{|\alpha|\le n}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}\sup_{t,a}|\partial_a^\alpha c|$, counting each multi-index once. Boundedness is separate: unbounded derivative sets have default real supremum zero, so the equality alone does not prove finiteness in the analytic sense.
p5.1.phase-independent-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm: For fixed spatial directions $d_i$, the order-$n$ expression sums one term for each nondecreasing derivative word of length at most $n$. Without Hölder terms, that term is the supremum of the corresponding derivative norm over the supplied time index and spatial domain. With Hölder terms, it is the maximum of that supremum and the half-Hölder seminorm. Equal-point quotients have value zero. The set whose real supremum is taken always includes zero; if it is unbounded above, its formal supremum is zero. Consequently these expressions are norms only when boundedness has been established. For $d_i=\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$, the expression is the scaled label norm; adding $h\partial_s$ gives the mixed label and phase norm. No time derivative occurs. For bounded smooth phase-independent $c$, taking the three directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ gives exactly the paper’s sum $\sum_{m\le n}\ell_*^m|c|_m$.
p5.1.phase-independent-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelDirection: The paper gives the entire finite norm of a phase-independent coefficient. This definition specifies only the three directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$; summing their mixed derivatives and discarding phase derivatives requires the other two declarations linked here.

p5.1.fixed-derivative-cost.TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound.weighted_: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\ell_*\ge0$, $p,c$ be nonnegative integers and $C_j\ge0$. Suppose a field satisfies $\|D_a^jf\|_\infty\le C_j\mathsf D^{pj+c}$ uniformly in time and $\ell_*\mathsf D^p\le1$. Then $\sum_{j=0}^n\ell_*^j\|D_a^jf\|_\infty\le(\sum_{j=0}^nC_j)\mathsf D^c$. The exponent $c$ is independent of $n$, although the finite sum of constants is not. The paper applies this arithmetic bound to its parent coefficients. The formal statement applies to any field with the given derivative estimates.

p5.1.coefficient-list.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef: Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Put $F=DX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=G^Tk_*$, and suppose $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda>0$ at $t_0\in[0,T]$. A sequence $C_m\ge0$, chosen before the flow, gives $\|D_a^m\Phi\|_\infty\le C_m\mathsf D^{16m+16}$ for every $m\ge0$ and every $\Phi\in\{F,G,M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa\}$. Unlike the numbered proposition, this analytic helper assumes the velocity derivative bounds directly and requires no pressure, residual or coercivity condition.
p5.1.coefficient-list.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Put $F=DX$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$. For $\mathcal C=\{F,F^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa\}$, one exponent $C$ gives $\|D^m\Phi\|_\infty\le C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$. For $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the sums $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j\Phi\|_\infty$ and $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j(f\circ X)\|_\infty$ are bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^C$ and $C_nA_f$, respectively.

p5.1.polynomial-coefficients.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef: The theorem assumes spatial derivative bounds for the parent velocity directly, together with bounds on its forward and inverse flow derivatives. It obtains $C_m\mathsf D^{16m+16}$ for each of the six fields $F,F^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa$, using the multilinear operator norm. The fixed exponent $16m+16$ gives the uniform polynomial dependence claimed in (5.6), without a pressure or residual hypothesis.
p5.1.polynomial-coefficients.TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound: `ParentLabelJetBound` records $\|D_a^mf(t,a)\|\le C_m\mathsf D^{pm+c}$ at every time and label for one supplied field $f$. The owner theorem uses it six times with the same exponents, once per coefficient in (5.6). The two parameters separate the power incurred per derivative from the power at order zero.
p5.1.polynomial-coefficients.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1: The numbered theorem proves polynomial bounds for all six coefficients of the actual parent flow. It also treats derivatives of $f\circ X$ and the corresponding radius-weighted sums. The pressure assumption is on the residual and the effective Hessian for a smooth periodic $p_U$, so the same coefficient conclusion applies without choosing the zero-mean Poisson normalization used in the paper.
p5.1.polynomial-coefficients.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp: The theorem assumes derivative bounds $C_j A\mathsf D^j$ on a supplied smooth field $f$. Composing with the forward label flow replaces the power $j$ by $6j$, with constants chosen before $f$ and the parent. This supplies the field-composition clause of Proposition 5.1. It uses multilinear operator norms, which are equivalent to the coordinate-derivative norms up to order-dependent constants.
p5.1.polynomial-coefficients.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The statement bounds the six actual label coefficients with an exponent linear in the derivative order. It also bounds $f\circ X$ for a spatially smooth field whose derivatives have size $C_m A_f\mathsf D^m$ and whose amplitude $A_f$ is nonnegative. The paired estimates use multilinear operator norms in place of sums of coordinate derivative suprema. At this fixed dimension the comparison changes only the constants for each order.

p5.1.composition.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp: This proves (5.7) with the explicit exponent $6m$; it requires only the displayed flow and velocity-derivative hypotheses, rather than the full truncated parent.
p5.1.composition.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The formal parent pressure is more general than the normalized Poisson pressure selected by the paper. Coordinate derivative sums and operator norms differ only by permitted order-dependent constants.
p5.1.composition.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o: The chain rule expresses the label derivatives of $f\circ X$ as products of derivatives of $f$ and the flow. The parent estimates bound these products by $C_m A_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$ with one exponent independent of the order. This implication takes Bernstein’s inequality and the coefficient calculus in Lemma D.2 as inputs.

p5.1.weighted-coefficients.TorusEuler.ParentLabelJetBound.weighted_: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\ell_*\ge0$, $C_j\ge0$ and nonnegative integers $p,c$ satisfy $\ell_*\mathsf D^p\le1$. From $\|D^jf\|_\infty\le C_j\mathsf D^{pj+c}$, the formal statement concludes $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^jf\|_\infty\le(\sum_{j\le n}C_j)\mathsf D^c$. It applies to an arbitrary field with supplied bounds. The paper’s display asserts such bounds for the six parent coefficients and for $f\circ X$; this summation result neither proves those derivative estimates nor composes with the flow.
p5.1.weighted-coefficients.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo: The statement is a weighted summation of given bounds. It does not itself establish the composition estimate for $f\circ X$. Only the second type of estimate in (5.8) is supplied, after the composition bound has already been proved.
p5.1.weighted-coefficients.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: For $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the sums $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j\Phi\|_\infty$ and $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j(f\circ X)\|_\infty$ are bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^C$ and $C_nA_f$, respectively. Both bounds in (5.8) are present. The parent pressure class is broader than the paper’s normalized Poisson choice.
p5.1.weighted-coefficients.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o: Each order-$j$ derivative in the finite label norm is multiplied by $\ell_*^j$. Taking $\ell_*$ small enough absorbs the parent power accumulated per derivative. The coefficient bound retains its order-zero parent power, while the composed field is bounded by $C_nA_f$. The implication assumes Bernstein’s inequality and Lemma D.2.

p5.1.bernstein-input.TorusEuler.exists_parentVelocityJetBound: The paper also displays the intermediate factor $\mathsf D^{k-1}\|DU\|_\infty$. The formal conclusion gives only the final $\mathsf D^k$ estimate, with the broader $4\mathsf D$ band.
p5.1.bernstein-input.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity: The paper also displays the intermediate factor $\mathsf D^{k-1}\|DU\|_\infty$. The formal conclusion gives only the final $\mathsf D^k$ estimate, with the broader $4\mathsf D$ band.

p5.1.variational-equation.TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.labelJets_evolv: The formal statement differentiates $X_t=U\circ X$ to give $(D_a^nX)_t=D_a^n(U\circ X)$, with continuity of these derivatives. The paper also separates $(DU\circ X)D_a^nX$ and the lower-order forcing. The linked composition identity supplies that additional decomposition.
p5.1.variational-equation.TorusEuler.iteratedFDeriv_comp_sub_linea: The formal statement is a spatial chain rule for $D^n(f\circ g)-Df(g)D^ng$, with $n>0$ and $n$ times differentiable maps. It gives the partition sum defining the lower-order forcing after taking $f=U$, $g=X$; the time-evolution equation for $X$ is a separate input.

p5.1.faa-di-bruno.TorusEuler.iteratedFDeriv_comp_sub_linea: Let $n\ge1$ and let $g$ and $f$ be $C^n$ at $a$ and $g(a)$, respectively. The formal chain rule writes $D^n(f\circ g)(a)-Df(g(a))D^ng(a)$ as the sum over ordered set partitions of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ into at least two nonempty blocks. The term for blocks $B_1,\ldots,B_k$ applies $D^kf(g(a))$ to the derivatives $D^{|B_i|}g(a)$ in the corresponding arguments. With $f=U(t,\cdot)$ and $g=X(t,\cdot)$, these are exactly the terms displayed in the paper, expressed as multilinear maps. Their multiplicities are recorded by the partitions. No time-evolution claim is part of this spatial identity.

p5.1.propagator-bound.TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_multilinea: The paper quotes the propagator bound alone. The formal conclusion is the resulting forced-solution estimate. The propagator bound is used in its proof.

p5.1.flow-recurrence.TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.norm_iteratedFD: The paper groups coordinate derivatives by their orders and takes suprema. Passing from the formal pointwise operator norms and ordered partitions to those sums changes only the order-dependent constant.

p5.1.flow-power.TorusEuler.exists_forward_flowJetBounds: Fix a nonnegative sequence $R_n$. For $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and a smooth unit-periodic velocity with flow $X$, assume $\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^kU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^k$ for every $2\le k\le n$. There are $C_n\ge0$, chosen before the parent, such that $\|D_a^nX\|_\infty\le C_n\mathsf D^{5n-4}$ for every $n\ge1$. These are multilinear operator norms, equivalent to the paper’s coordinate sums up to order-dependent constants. Exponent subtraction is among nonnegative integers. The asserted range $n\ge1$ makes $5n-4$ the ordinary integer value.

p5.1.partition-power.TorusEuler.flowJet_partitionPower_le: The formal statement proves the final inequality $\mathsf D^2\mathsf D^k\prod_i\mathsf D^{5n_i-4}\le\mathsf D^{5n-4}$ for $\mathsf D\ge1$ and a partition into at least two positive parts. It does not separately state the intermediate exponent equalities displayed in the paper.

p5.1.jacobian-power.TorusEuler.norm_iteratedFDeriv_labelJaco: For any map $Y:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, label $a$, integer $n\ge0$, real $\mathsf D$ and sequence $C_j$, assume $\|D^{n+1}Y(a)\|\le C_{n+1}\mathsf D^{5(n+1)-4}$. Then $\|D^n(DY)(a)\|\le C_{n+1}\mathsf D^{5n+1}$. Both norms are multilinear operator norms. The formal statement imposes no smoothness hypothesis: the derivative expressions are defined everywhere, with value zero where the required derivative does not exist. In the smooth flow application they are ordinary derivatives. The exponent subtraction is performed among nonnegative integers; because $n+1\ge1$, it equals the displayed ordinary integer subtraction. The formal implication requires the preceding flow estimate as input and does not itself prove that estimate.

p5.1.remaining-coefficients.TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficientJetB: The paper describes the successive product and inverse rules. The formal statement records their resulting bounds, rather than an assertion that particular proof rules are applicable.

p5.1.weighting-composed-field.TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo: The paper displays the bound for one derivative order of an already composed field. The formal statement gives the whole finite sum for an arbitrary field satisfying the supplied derivative bounds.

p5.1.residual-weighted.TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted: The Fourier band $4\mathsf D$ controls spatial derivatives of the residual by Bernstein, and the flow bounds control the derivatives created by composing with $X$. The small label radius absorbs those extra powers of $\mathsf D$, leaving $C_n\lambda^{-5/2}$ in the finite norm. This field estimate also applies to other fields with the same band and amplitude.

p5.2.mean-equation.TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution: On $[0,T]$, let $F,G,M$ be smooth unit-periodic matrix fields with $GF=FG=I$, $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Put $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. For a supplied label force $f_{\rm lab}$, a smooth mean solution consists of smooth unit-periodic fields $v,z,B,\mathsf q$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $B=Fv$ and $B_t+MB+G^T\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\rm lab}$ on the closed interval. These are defining conditions, not an existence assertion. No spatial mean normalization of $\mathsf q$ is imposed. An actual flow is not part of these data. Only after separately identifying $F=D_aX$, $M=DU\circ X$ and $f_{\rm lab}=f\circ X$ may one interpret $Fz$ as particle displacement and $B\circ X^{-1}$ as the Eulerian correction. The paper additionally identifies $F$ with a volume-preserving flow derivative and writes the transported divergence condition. Arbitrary matrix data in this definition do not by themselves justify that geometric interpretation.
p5.2.mean-equation.TorusEuler.trace_endpointPhysicalMean_eq: The paper gives the full mean equation, both endpoint conditions and $B=DXz_t$. This formal statement supplies only $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, assuming volume preservation, $B=DXv$ and $\operatorname{div}_av=0$. It neither imposes the time equation nor asserts either displacement endpoint.
p5.2.mean-equation.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution: It defines a mean solution rather than constructing one. For the supplied volume-preserving flow, the Piola identity makes the formal condition $\operatorname{div}_av=0$ equivalent to the paper’s transported divergence condition.

p5.2.mean-coordinate-readout.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution: The paper identifies both $g=DX^T\bar f$ and $v=z_t$. This formal condition supplies $z_t=v$ and $B=DXv$ with zero displacement endpoints and divergence-free $v$; it does not define $g$. The other linked statement defines the transformed forcing.
p5.2.mean-coordinate-readout.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14: Put $v=F^{-1}B=z_t$ and $g=F^T\bar f$. Thus the displayed transformed source and label velocity are explicitly the ones used in the estimate.

p5.2.initial-velocity-selected.TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.mean_: On $[0,T]$, let $F,G,M$ be smooth unit-periodic matrix fields with $GF=FG=I$, $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Put $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Assume $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, $L\ge0$. For fixed smooth periodic $f_{\rm lab}$, any two smooth solutions $B_i=F(z_i)_t$, $\operatorname{div}(z_i)_t=0$, $z_i(0)=z_i(T)=0$, $B_{i,t}+MB_i+G^T\nabla\mathsf q_i=f_{\rm lab}$ have $B_1=B_2$ on $[0,T]$. This gives uniqueness of the full mean, hence its initial value. It does not prescribe that initial value or establish existence.

p5.2.source-derivative-loss.TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis: The paper describes a derivative loss for the mean source. The formal inequality concerns any smooth field with finite norms: $\|f\|_{[n]}\le\|f\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$, for $0<\ell_*\le1$. Applying it to the transformed source after the endpoint estimate yields the stated loss.

p5.2.all-solutions.TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns: Put $F=DX$, $M=DU\circ X$ and require $\|M\|\le L\le\mathsf D$, $L\ge0$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. The estimate applies to every existing smooth endpoint solution for the force. No special construction of that solution is assumed.
p5.2.all-solutions.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The quantifier is over every smooth endpoint mean solution for the supplied force. Existence of such a solution is a separate theorem.

p5.2.mean-estimate.TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns: This helper uses direct velocity-derivative and coercivity hypotheses and the explicit exponent $b+2+2s$; the paper packages them into its truncated parent and writes a common absolute exponent after fixing the radius.
p5.2.mean-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The formal pressure hypothesis permits any smooth periodic $p_U$ satisfying these bounds. The paper’s normalized Poisson pressure is a special case. This broader parent class accounts for the stronger claim.
p5.2.mean-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2: The formal pressure hypothesis permits any smooth periodic $p_U$ satisfying these bounds. The paper’s normalized Poisson pressure is a special case. This broader parent class accounts for the stronger claim.

p5.2.mean-coefficient-powers.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p: Assuming Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.2, there are nonnegative sequences $C_K(m),C_\Omega(m)$ and nonnegative integers $a_K,a_\Omega$, fixed before the parent, such that $\|D_a^mK\|_\infty\le C_K(m)\mathsf D^{a_K(m+1)}$ and $\|D_a^m\Omega\|_\infty\le C_\Omega(m)\mathsf D^{a_\Omega(m+1)}$ for every $m\ge0$. The implication is conditional on the two cited results. It does not itself prove Proposition 5.1 or Lemma D.2.

p5.2.inverse-constant-power.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound: The full sentence also requires applying Theorem 4.2 and identifying the four quantities with the parent coefficient bounds. Neither analytic step is concluded by this arithmetic declaration.

p5.2.radius-threshold.TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanWeightedCoef: The second inequality involving the inverse bound $A$ is absent. It requires choosing the radius from a separately obtained polynomial bound for $A$.
p5.2.radius-threshold.TorusEuler.meanScalarRadius_absorbs_inve: This arithmetic statement assumes $A\le\mathsf D^a$ and a radius $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$ with $s\ge2(a+9)$, and proves $A\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}\le1$. It does not estimate derivatives of $K$ or $\Omega$, so it supplies only the smallness step in (5.13).
p5.2.radius-threshold.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: If the supplied bound $A$ is at most $\mathsf D^{C_A}$, choose the envelope exponent large enough that the factor $\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}$ is at most $1/A$. This gives the scaled half-Hölder coefficient bound at every positive order with order-dependent constants. The statement applies to any positive $A$ under the polynomial bound, and the endpoint inverse supplies the application’s value of $A$.
p5.2.radius-threshold.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13: For every $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$ and every integer $m\ge1$, the formal statement gives finite coefficient half-Hölder norms and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$. The paper uses its particular endpoint inverse constant. The formal statement covers every positive $A$ with the given polynomial bound and permits a broader parent pressure class. It does not prove that $A$ bounds an inverse.
p5.2.radius-threshold.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of: The coefficient calculus and the half-Hölder comparison leave the factor $\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}$ after radius weighting at every positive order. Choose one envelope exponent so that this factor is at most $1/A$, using the supplied polynomial bound on $A$. The implication assumes Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and (D.2).

p5.2.mean-lifting-coefficients.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe: The separate factors $4$ and $2T$ in the coefficient condition express the two contributions. The formal conclusion is the derivative estimate, not a separate norm calculation for time integration.

p5.2.derivative-lifting.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The abstract lifting lemma obtains higher spatial estimates by differentiating the equation and controlling the terms from differentiated coefficients. The mean equation applies that estimate with the endpoint solution space and the time primitive $L=-\int_0^t g(t\prime)\,\mathrm dt\prime$. The lifting lemma itself takes its operator and source as inputs.
p5.2.derivative-lifting.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of: Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. The substitution $L=-Jg$ is a step in its proof, not its displayed conclusion.

p5.2.holder-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14: The derivative order is unchanged. The explicit finiteness premise is satisfied by the paper’s smooth periodic fields. The broader admissible pressure class gives the stronger comparison; no Poisson or mean-zero pressure requirement is added.
p5.2.holder-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14: The derivative order is unchanged. The explicit finiteness premise is satisfied by the paper’s smooth periodic fields. The broader admissible pressure class gives the stronger comparison; no Poisson or mean-zero pressure requirement is added.
p5.2.holder-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of: The lemma passes from the inverse at order zero to the scaled half-Hölder estimate for the normalized velocity $v$. Its source is $g=F^T\bar f$ at the same derivative order. The implication uses the endpoint inverse, the parent coefficient bounds, the Hölder comparison and the radius bound (5.13) as premises.

p5.2.product-readout.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o: The exported bound for $B$ comes from applying the estimate for $v$ to $g=F^T\bar f$ and multiplying back by $F$. The formal proof bounds the products in a scaled supremum norm at one higher order and then applies the half-Hölder comparison. The passage describes the intermediate same-order Hölder product estimate.

p5.2.fixed-power-readout.TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis: For a smooth field with bounded derivative sets, $0<\ell_*\le1$ and any $n\ge0$, the formal inequality is $\|f\|_{[n]}\le\|f\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$. These are sums of scaled label derivatives, uniform in the supplied time index. The middle norm uses the maximum of supremum and half-Hölder seminorm. It does not mention the mean equation. The estimates for $B=Fv$ and $g=F^T\bar f$ must first be supplied to obtain (5.12).
p5.2.fixed-power-readout.TorusEuler.meanScalarBudget_le_power: Suppose $A\le C\mathsf D^a$ and $B\le KA(\mathsf D^b/\sqrt{\mathsf D^{-s}})^2(F/\sqrt{\mathsf D^{-s}})$. The inequality concerns real numbers; identifying them with the mean, source and inverse bounds is required separately.
p5.2.fixed-power-readout.TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns: There exist integers $b,s_0\ge0$ and constants $C_n\ge0$, chosen before the flow, such that for $s\ge s_0$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^{b+2+2s}\|f_{\rm lab}\|_{[n+1]}$. The loss of one source derivative and the final fixed parent power are the conclusion of this analytic theorem.

e02.transverse.forward-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve: Assume smooth phase-independent strain and nonzero covector with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, and smooth source profiles on $[0,T]$ compatible with phase and label translations. This is the solution of (5.15) used at each level of the expansion: its velocity starts from zero and its pressure has zero phase mean. It is selected from the proved existence result for a smooth source with zero phase mean.

e02.transverse.inactive-source.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: The solution starts from $V(0)=0$. If the forcing vanishes through a given time, each phase at each label solves the homogeneous linear equation there and the velocity stays zero. The pressure obtained from its normalized phase primitive then vanishes on the same prefix.

e02.transverse.weight.TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN: The velocity norm divides each scaled pointwise derivative by $\gamma(t)>0$ before taking its supremum. In the application $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, so the norm compares the correction to the central amplitude at the same time. The norm sums over one copy of each label and phase multi-index.
e02.transverse.weight.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm: For a smooth profile $f$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, define $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}=\sum_{|\alpha|+j\le n}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup_{t\in[t_0,T],a,s}|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^jf(t,a,s)|/\gamma(t)$ for positive scales and positive $\gamma$. The unrestricted expression instead uses $|\gamma(t)^{-1}|$: division by zero is assigned zero, and an unbounded set of real derivative values has real supremum assigned zero. Consequently the unrestricted formula alone does not certify boundedness. The positivity and regularity hypotheses in the estimates are essential.

e02.transverse.equation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: For smooth zero-mean forcing and smooth phase-independent coefficients with nonzero $\kappa$ satisfying $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, the formal statement constructs a solution of (5.15). It additionally fixes $V(0)=0$ and zero phase mean for the pressure, and records support and conditional reflection properties.
e02.transverse.equation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans: The formal condition includes the momentum equation, transversality and zero phase mean of the velocity, together with $V(0)=0$, normalized pressure, its phase-derivative formula and support and reflection consequences. The forcing is assumed centered by the existence theorem. The displayed equations alone do not list all these additional requirements.
e02.transverse.equation.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution: The formal condition includes (5.15) for smooth phase-periodic profiles, and additionally fixes $V(0)=0$ and zero phase mean for the pressure. Zero phase average of the source follows from the centered velocity and phase-independent coefficients. It is also an explicit premise in the estimate where this condition is used.

e02.transverse.pressure-slope.TorusEuler.norm_sq_mul_oscillatoryPressu: For $\kappa\ne0$, multiplying the scalar defined by `oscillatoryPressureSlope` by $|\kappa|^2$ cancels its denominator and gives $\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV$. The lemma is algebraic. The transverse solve separately identifies the scalar with $\partial_s\mathsf p$ by constructing the zero-mean phase primitive. That identification gives the pressure equation (5.16).

e02.transverse.projected-ode.TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a: The formal statement equates the projected right-hand side with $f-MV-q\kappa$, where $q=(\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV)/|\kappa|^2$. It contains no time derivative and asserts no solution. With the pressure-slope identity and momentum equation, it yields (5.17). At $\kappa=0$, reciprocal powers are assigned zero.

e02.transverse.zero-start-pressure.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans: The transverse solution consists of a velocity $V$ and pressure $\mathsf p$ satisfying (5.15), with $V(0)=0$ and zero phase mean for the pressure. Its pressure is the normalized primitive specified by (5.16). The formulation also records the support and reflection properties used in §5.5: vanishing of the source before activation or outside a label set passes to both fields. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
e02.transverse.zero-start-pressure.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve: Assume smooth phase-independent strain and nonzero covector with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, and smooth source profiles on $[0,T]$ compatible with phase and label translations. This is the solution of (5.15) used at each level of the expansion: its velocity starts from zero and its pressure has zero phase mean. It is selected from the proved existence result for a smooth source with zero phase mean. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.

e02.transverse.smooth-unique.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: The paper asserts both existence of a smooth solution and uniqueness. This formal statement provides the smooth solution without a uniqueness conclusion. The separate uniqueness result linked here supplies the remaining assertion.
e02.transverse.smooth-unique.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: The formal statement identifies two smooth transverse solutions with the same source, the same parent and interval, zero initial velocity and zero-mean pressure. It proves uniqueness but does not construct a smooth solution. The other linked theorem supplies existence and regularity.

e02.transverse.constraints.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: Pairing the transverse equation with the transported covector shows that $\kappa\cdot V$ stays zero. Taking the phase mean gives a homogeneous equation for the mean velocity because the coefficients are independent of phase and the source is centered. The zero initial value gives $\langle V\rangle_s=0$.

e02.transverse.support.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: Fix a label where the forcing is zero at all times and phases. At this label the zero-initial transverse solution is zero by uniqueness, so the formula for the pressure slope also vanishes. Phase normalization fixes the pressure itself at zero there. This transfers the label support of the forcing to both output profiles.

e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans: The formal condition passes vanishing of the source for $t<t_0$ to vanishing of velocity and pressure there, and separately fixes $V(0)=0$. At $t_0>0$, continuity supplies the value at $t=t_0$; that endpoint implication is the separate theorem linked here.
e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer: The formal statement gives the value zero at $t=t_0$ from continuity and vanishing before it, with $0<t_0\le T$. It assumes preactivation vanishing and does not derive it from the forcing. If $t_0=0$, the prescribed initial value supplies the endpoint instead.
e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: The formal statement constructs a smooth solution and passes source vanishing to the solution for $t<t_0$. The value at a positive activation time then follows from continuity; at $t_0=0$ it follows from the separately prescribed zero initial value.

e02.transverse.forward-frame.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif: The paper chooses an orthonormal basis of $k_*^\perp$ and writes a map from $\mathbb R^2$. The formal definition restricts $D_aX$ directly to the Euclidean subspace $k_*^\perp$. For nonzero $k_*$, choosing such a basis identifies the two maps isometrically.

e02.transverse.inverse-frame.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul: The formal definition is $\Pi_{k_*^\perp}G(I-P_{G^Tk_*})$, with $G$ an arbitrary linear map. When $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$ it is the inverse on the transported transverse plane after orthogonal projection, equivalent to the paper’s Gram-matrix formula after choosing orthonormal coordinates.

e02.transverse.frame-identities.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframe_id: The formal statement proves the two identities assuming mutually inverse maps $F,G$, with $\kappa=G^Tk_*$. Its first identity acts on the subspace $k_*^\perp$, whereas the paper writes $\mathbb R^2$ in a chosen orthonormal basis. For $k_*\ne0$ these are the same Euclidean plane in different representations.

e02.transverse.frame-time.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif: For fixed $k_*$ and a differentiable deformation $F(t)$ satisfying $F_t=MF$, restrict $F$ to $k_*^\perp$. The transported frame satisfies $\partial_tA_\perp=MA_\perp$ whenever the full deformation satisfies its corresponding evolution equation. This follows by restricting the deformation to the fixed transverse plane. In §5.4 the identity turns the equation for $V=A_\perp v$ into the fixed-plane equation (5.18), including the factor two in its coefficient.

e02.transverse.coordinate-equation.TorusEuler.fixedTransverseGenerator: The formal definition gives the generator $-2A_\perp^\dagger MA_\perp$ on an abstract fixed space. The paper also asserts the transformed differential equation and the forcing $A_\perp^\dagger f$. Those identifications require the frame identities and its evolution. The definition alone supplies only the coefficient, with its sign moved to the right-hand side.

e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.paper_hier: The input seed already carries a relative amplitude comparison and a positive normalized coupling bound near the origin; neither is inferred from smoothness alone. On $[t_0,T]$ and $\lVert a\rVert\le2\ell_*$, the localized seed satisfies $\lVert\mathbf a(t,a)\rVert\le2\lVert\mathbf a(t,0)\rVert$ and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a>0$. These are exactly the two conclusions of (5.19). This result draws them from an already constructed seed with quantitative localization bounds. It does not repeat that construction.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The near-origin clause retains exactly the upper amplitude bound and strict positive coupling. Its parent pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying the residual and coercivity bounds, and the central amplitude need only remain nonzero and below $\lambda^{-3/4}$; the paper fixes the Poisson pressure and an attained normalization.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3: The near-origin clause retains exactly the upper amplitude bound and strict positive coupling. Its parent pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying the residual and coercivity bounds, and the central amplitude need only remain nonzero and below $\lambda^{-3/4}$; the paper fixes the Poisson pressure and an attained normalization.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: The paper displays an upper amplitude bound and strict positivity of the coupling in (5.19). The formal result also gives relative seed error, a lower amplitude bound and quantitative coupling bounds, so it contains additional information about the localized seed.

e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: The statement takes smooth active-interval fields with $V$ transverse and satisfying the projected wave equation. It also requires the initial value and source to vanish off a closed set within $2\ell_*$ of the lattice, with period-one phase and the prescribed label-phase translation symmetry. The parent deformation and central-wave bounds are separate inputs.
e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The paper allows $V$ and $f$ to be smooth only on $[t_0,T]$. The formal statement requires fields smooth on all of $[0,T]$ and then restricts the estimate to the active interval, so this statement alone covers a narrower class of data.

e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: The order-$n$ norm of a supported transverse solution on $[t_0,T]$ is bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^{20}$ times the sum of the launch norm divided by $\gamma(t_0)$ and the active weighted source norm. The exponent $20$ is fixed for every derivative order. In this estimate $V$ already solves the forward equation.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: For a small enough radius, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, supported solutions satisfy $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. The paper gives (5.20) for fields defined only on the active interval. This formal estimate uses fields smooth on all of $[0,T]$, so the numerical bound is retained under a stronger time-domain assumption.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. The paper gives (5.20) for fields smooth on $[t_0,T]$. The numbered formal statement assumes smoothness on $[0,T]$ before restricting to the active interval; its conclusion therefore does not by itself cover arbitrary active-interval data.

e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a nonzero central seed with relative transverse growth at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfy phase and coupled lattice periodicity; support lies within $2\ell_*$ of lattice points. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed satisfy $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$ and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ must obey $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling.

r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The strain and nonzero covector are smooth and phase independent, with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$; source profiles satisfy the phase period and the coupled label-translation law. For a smooth source with zero phase mean, this result constructs a transverse solution of (5.15) with zero initial velocity and normalized pressure. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: The paper refers to the solution and its pressure. This theorem proves that two smooth solutions with the same forcing, zero initial velocity and zero phase mean for the pressure coincide. The existence theorem linked here supplies the pair.

e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a nonzero central seed with relative transverse growth at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. For a small enough radius, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, supported solutions satisfy $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. If the centered forcing vanishes before activation, its zero-initial solution also satisfies $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$. Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfy phase and coupled lattice periodicity; support lies within $2\ell_*$ of lattice points. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The formal bound retains $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}$ for every zero-initial transverse solution with supported, centered forcing. It allows the broader parent pressure class and any nonzero central amplitude below $\lambda^{-3/4}$, without requiring the peak normalization in the paper.

e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_pap: For a supplied localized seed with smooth compatible continuation, the fixed radial envelope shape at every such radius gives $\|A_1\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p[A_1]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}\lambda^{-5/4}$. The paper states (5.22) for its fixed admissible radial cutoff. The formal estimate uses one chosen envelope, so it preserves the bound for that choice without quantifying over every admissible cutoff.
e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The paper allows any fixed radial cutoff with the stated plateau and support. The formal leading-wave clause uses a particular admissible choice, retaining (5.22) for that envelope.

e02.lemma53.frame-bounds.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra: The formal statement gives $\|A_\perp\|\le\|D_aX\|$ for a restricted linear map. It treats the first bound only; inserting the parent deformation bound yields $\|A_\perp\|\le\mathsf D$.
The formal statement bounds the projected inverse by $\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|$. It treats the second inequality only. The parent inverse-deformation hypothesis gives the bound by $\mathsf D$.

e02.lemma53.coframe-coefficient-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra: Given Lemma D.2’s product estimate and smooth coefficient bounds $\|D^jc\|\le W_j\mathsf D^{16(j+1)}$, the formal conclusion bounds $G(I-P_\kappa)$ and $-2G(I-P_\kappa)MF$ with exponents $32(j+1)$ and $64(j+1)$. The paper uses the Gram-matrix inverse in coordinates on $\mathbb R^2$. The forward frame is not separately bounded by this declaration, and no inverse relation between $F,G$ is assumed.

e02.lemma53.gronwall.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forward: The formal statement treats any real normed-space homogeneous equation with a positive continuously differentiable weight, a central propagation factor $K>0$, coefficient perturbation at most $K^{-1}$ and interval length at most one. It gives factor $eK$; the paper’s application takes $K=\mathsf D^3$.

e02.lemma53.forced-integral.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forced_no: The formal estimate applies to a general forced linear equation with continuous coefficients and forcing, positive continuously differentiable weight and perturbation at most $K^{-1}$ of a central equation with propagation factor $K$. Setting $K=\mathsf D^3$ and the initial time to $t_0$ gives the paper’s displayed bound.

e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: The paper bounds the relative seed error by $C\mathsf D^C\lVert a\rVert$. The formal conclusion gives an unspecified coefficient depending on $\mathsf D$, so its statement does not expose the uniform polynomial dependence used in this display.
e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear: The paper requires the relative-error coefficient to be an absolute power of $\mathsf D$. The formal condition leaves that coefficient free, so this condition alone does not assert the displayed polynomial dependence.

e02.lemma53.word-lifting.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeWordBound_of: The formal implication obtains bounds for all ordered parameter derivatives of a smooth linear ordinary differential equation from Lemma D.3, a weighted homogeneous propagation bound, initial and source bounds, and bounds for positive-order coefficient derivatives. Its amplification factor depends on derivative order and the coefficient bound times the interval length and propagation factor; no smallness is assumed. The paper’s sentence identifies the particular transverse equation to which this general result is applied.

e02.lemma53.weight-after-derivatives.TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN: Apply the label and phase derivatives to the profile first, scale them by powers of the envelope radius and phase width, and divide by the positive value $\gamma(t)$. The time-dependent weight is never differentiated in this norm. Taking the supremum after division is what yields the relative estimate in (5.20).

e02.lemma53.pressure-coefficient-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu: The formal statement bounds only $M(\ell_*a)$, $\kappa(\ell_*a)/\lambda$ and $\lambda^2/|\kappa(\ell_*a)|^2$, through each fixed order, by $C\mathsf D,C\mathsf D^2,C\mathsf D^4$. It assumes smooth coefficient bounds at scale $\mathsf D_0$, $\mathsf D_0^{64}\le\mathsf D$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^{16}\le1$. The product and phase-primitive estimates invoked in the paper are still needed to obtain the pressure bound.

e02.lemma53.pressure-estimate.TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_weig: The formal bound controls weighted derivatives of the normalized phase primitive using supplied coefficient, velocity and source bounds, for smooth centered one-periodic fields. It retains those coefficient constants explicitly. Inserting the parent estimates and summing the derivative bounds gives $C_n\mathsf D^C$ in (5.24). This theorem alone does not derive that parent power.

e02.lemma53.leading-proof-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le: The paper obtains the leading estimate by applying (5.20) with zero forcing, followed by (5.24). The formal proof uses a separate homogeneous leading-wave estimate instead, so this step reaches the same bound without invoking those already assembled conclusions.

e02.lemma53.leading-homogeneous.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap: With $A_1=g\mathbf a F_h$ and $\mathsf p[A_1]=-2g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)|\kappa|^{-2}P_h$, the formal statement proves $A_{1,t}+MA_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p[A_1]=0$ on $[t_0,T]$. The paper states the homogeneous transverse identity for any fixed admissible cutoff. The formal statement proves it for the chosen envelope, a special case of the paper's statement.

e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The formal definition only reindexes a stored correction: the paper’s $C_p$ is stored at $p-1$. It does not assert $C_1=0$ or the total velocity formula. The first follows from the expansion conditions and the latter from the other linked equality.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The formal definition gives $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ with the shifted correction index. It supplies this component of the display, but neither $Z_p$ nor the total velocity nor $C_1=0$.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. The formal definition gives $Z_p=Y_p+B_p$. The other equalities and the convention $C_1=0$ are separate definitions or hypotheses.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq: The formal equality gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$ for $P\ge1$, assuming $C_1=0$. The paper also lists the definitions of $Y_p,Z_p$ and states the convention. This theorem uses rather than proves that convention.

e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous: The paper asserts a bound for $C_p$. The linked formal result checks only that the frequency exponents fit. The estimate of the correction itself is a separate step.
e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The definition groups $V_p$ with the preceding curl correction as $Y_p=V_p+C_p$. It does not prove the frequency gain or the norm bound justifying that grouping; Lemma 5.5 and the exponent calculation supply those facts.

e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: The formal definition gives the general source at level two using the differentiated switched correction, and subtracts its activation term. Identifying it with the displayed unswitched expression requires the leading-wave cutoff identities. The definition alone does not state those time-derivative identities.
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.levelSource_eq_s: The formal equality reconciles two finite-sum definitions of $H_p$ for $p\le P$. It does not itself turn the level-two linear term into the unswitched expression in (5.25). The leading-wave activation identity is still required.
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: The formal definition gives the general source at level two using the differentiated switched correction, and subtracts its activation term. Identifying it with the displayed unswitched expression requires the leading-wave cutoff identities. The definition alone does not state those time-derivative identities.

e02.hierarchy.first-linear-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: At level two the relay contains the switched leading correction and pressure and the subtracted activation correction. All these profiles have zero phase mean, and the cutoff and linear coefficient fields are phase independent. Averaging therefore removes the whole linear relay before the first mean solve.

e02.hierarchy.mean-fast-integration.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: The paper applies phase integration by parts with $C_2=C[V_1]$ and the second factor also $V_1$. The formal statement allows any transverse zero-mean $V$ and an independent profile $Y$, giving the same identity for $C[V]$ and $Y$.

e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: The definition inserts $-R_U\circ X$ at level two and nowhere else. It does not bound that residual by $C_n\lambda^{-5/2}$; the other linked estimate supplies the analytic reason for including it at this level.
e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted: The estimate takes a field $R$ of Fourier radius $4\mathsf D$ and size $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Under the parent flow bounds and $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$, its composition with $X$ stays within $C_n\lambda^{-5/2}$ in the scaled label norm. Applying this to $R_U$ controls its size in the mean equation. The separate definition `meanSource` determines that $-R_U\circ X$ enters at level two.

e02.hierarchy.quadratic-levels.TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel: The two indices and the shift are nonnegative integers, so subtraction is truncated at zero. Positive interaction indices make this agree with ordinary subtraction in the paper’s uses. Label advection of levels $i$ and $j$ is assigned level $i+j$, while phase advection is assigned level $i+j-1$. This is the counting convention before (5.26). It determines which terms are canceled at the current level and which survive in the remainder; numerical estimates for these terms are proved later.

e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). The quoted formula is the case $3\le p\le P$; the formal level-two definition additionally subtracts the activation correction.
e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: Here a stored correction at index $p-1$ is the paper’s $C_p$; subtraction of indices is truncated at zero, and the physical use is $p\ge2$. The quoted formula is the case $3\le p\le P$; the formal level-two definition additionally subtracts the activation correction.

e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource: `oscSource` subtracts the phase average from $H_p$ and negates the result. This gives the forcing $f_p$ that cancels the oscillatory part of $H_p$. The separate mean-source definition supplies $-\langle H_p\rangle_s$ and the level-two parent residual. The supplemental oscillatory source $f_p^S$ uses the mean after it has been solved.
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: The formal definition gives the mean source $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$. It does not define the centered oscillatory source $f_p$ in the same display. That part is supplied by the separate oscillatory-source definition.
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The formal definition gives the mean source $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$. e02.hierarchy.pre-source-known.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: The comparison is algebraic for fixed operators, fixed depth and identical activation error; no solution estimate is assumed. Two profile families agreeing at every earlier level produce the same $H_p$ for $p\ge2$. Their divergence corrections are included in that agreement, each having already been determined from the preceding oscillation. This makes precise the sentence before (5.28): the preliminary source requires none of the new fields $V_p$, $B_p$, or $\mathsf p_p$.

e02.hierarchy.mean-before-transverse.TorusEuler.FiniteHierarchySolvers.constr: The formal statement identifies the recursively chosen $B_p,\bar q_p$ with the output of a supplied mean solution operator for $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$. It does not establish solvability of the physical endpoint problem. That must already be supplied to this algebraic construction.

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.meanPhaseA: The formal statement gives the positive advection sum $\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$ for $p\le P$. The supplementary source in the paper is its negative. The other linked definition supplies that sign.

e02.hierarchy.transverse-after-mean.TorusEuler.FiniteHierarchySolvers.constr: The formal statement identifies the recursively selected pair with the output of a supplied transverse solution operator for exactly $f_p+f_p^S$, whose average is zero. Existence of that physical operator is an input here, not a conclusion of this selection theorem.

r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: The formal condition requires $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$ for retained levels. It does not retain $Q_p$ as a separate member of the family. r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The formal definition reindexes the stored correction as the paper’s $C_{p+1}$. It imposes neither $Q_p=Q[V_p]$ nor $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$; the latter is a separate expansion condition.

e02.hierarchy.order-required.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.meanPhaseA: The level-$p$ supplemental source is determined once the means through level $p$ and the preceding oscillatory blocks are fixed. The formal equality gives the supplementary advection sum before its negative sign is applied; its last term is the one involving $B_p$ and $Y_1$. Identifying $Y_1=V_1$ uses $C_1=0$, and the dependence on already computed fields is the separate congruence result linked here.

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: The profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one; $\langle\cdot\rangle_s$ denotes integration over one phase period. The phase average of $(B\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is zero whenever $B$ and $\kappa$ are phase independent and $Y$ is periodic. No zero-mean condition on $Y$ is needed for this identity. Applying it to each term of (5.28) proves that the supplementary source is admissible for the transverse equation.

e02.hierarchy.reflection.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const: The paper asserts reflection symmetry of its constructed profiles. The explicit zero means of $V_p$ and $C_p$ therefore leave exactly the sum of $B_p$ as the mean of $W$. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.oscillatory-support.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The assertion gives $W-\langle W\rangle_s=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1})$ and makes it vanish outside the envelope support. The first oscillation vanishes by the cutoff, and the transverse solves at later levels preserve this zero prefix. The support clause ranges over the oscillatory fields and their sources, while the mean equations use the full time interval. e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The correction generated by $V_P$ is retained at the last index. With $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$, both $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ are that correction. In the helper whose array stores $C[V_p]$ at index $p$, the stored $C_P$ is the paper’s $C_{P+1}$. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: For $1\le p\le P$, $C_{p+1}=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_p/|\kappa|^2)]$. For $2\le p\le P$, require $B_{p,t}+MB_p+\mathbf d\bar q_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$ and $V_{p,t}+MV_p+\kappa\mathsf p_{p,s}=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)+f_p^S$. Here $H_p$ is the sum of the preceding linear correction and all lower-level quadratic interactions, with the activation correction subtracted at level two; $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_s(V_{p+1-i}+C_{p+1-i})$. Means satisfy $B_p=DX\,z_{p,t}$, $\operatorname{div}_az_{p,t}=0$, $z_p(0)=z_p(T)=0$ and zero spatial pressure mean. Finally $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The correction generated by $V_P$ is retained at the last index. With $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$, both $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ are that correction. In the helper whose array stores $C[V_p]$ at index $p$, the stored $C_P$ is the paper’s $C_{P+1}$. e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proved numbered theorem gives T1 for every stage of the selected construction. In particular the Fourier support is bounded after the wave and corrections are assembled, since the stage is the output of the prescribed cutoff.

e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: T2 is required of the sequence produced for an admissible threshold and sufficiently large $N$. e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof obtains all three estimates for the same stage and the same flow. The inverse deformation bound uses the reverse flow at the transported point. The residual bound is on the actual Euler momentum defect of that selected velocity and pressure.
