e03-s7-all-orders.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_tends: The formal theorem gives $q_j\to\infty$ from the greatest-order recurrence, $q_1=1$, $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$, and monotone unbounded frequencies. It needs neither monotonicity of $\mathcal B$ nor its logarithmic floor. The paper's parameter schedule supplies these assumptions and therefore has the claimed eventual growth.
e03-s7-all-orders.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3: For the frequency and greatest-order recurrence (1.14), $b\ge1$, positive threshold values and the logarithmic floor (1.13), the formal Lemma 1.3 proves $q_j\to\infty$. Hence for every fixed integer $m$, all sufficiently late orders exceed $m$ in this one construction.

r5-ind-figure4-inactive.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The caption depicts $i\ge4$. The formal theorem identifies the expansion oscillation and proves $O_i=0$ on $[0,t_i]$ for every $i\ge2$, so it covers the depicted stages and also the two earlier indices.

r5-ind-figure4-crossing.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce: For each later wave in a supplied construction, the central-wave data identify the selected physical crossing with the next activation time. The internal index zero refers to wave two, so its crossing is $t_3$. This identifies the end of the caption's segment. It does not assert that the intermediate fields are exact Euler solutions.

r5-ind-figure4-endpoint.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The formal theorem supplies a smooth approximate velocity on $[0,S_i]$ at every stage, and a positive common limit $T_\infty<S_i$. The residual is small rather than required to vanish, so “solution” in this caption means the stated approximate solution, not an exact Euler continuation through blow-up.

e03-s7-residual-support.TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_: For a smooth velocity with Fourier support at most $2\Lambda_j$ on the entire closed interval, the formal theorem assumes the projected momentum identity with a continuous residual and the advective term represented in the spatial one-half Hölder space. It then proves that residual has support at most $4\Lambda_j$. This is the stated conclusion under the stage equation, not a bound for an arbitrary independently chosen residual.

r2-s7-bernstein-input.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1: The supplied formal Lemma B.1 contains Bernstein bounds for band-limited fields. To obtain these two bounds one must additionally use the stage velocity and residual sizes and their respective bands $2\Lambda_j$ and $4\Lambda_j$. Those substitutions are not themselves conclusions of Lemma B.1.

e03-s7-low-gradient.TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds: For sufficiently large $\lambda_j$, the formal theorem assumes joint smoothness, velocity size $\lambda_j$, frequency band $2\lambda_j^5$, residual size $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$, and the projected momentum equation. It concludes the two pointwise derivative bounds, uniformly on the closed interval. Time derivatives at its endpoints are taken within that interval, and matrix norms are operator norms.

r2-s7-step-inputs.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: The formal step requirements use exactly the parent $U_{j-1}$, frequency $\lambda_j$, activation $t_j$, endpoint $S_j$, parent bound $\lambda_{j-1}^9$ and Fourier cutoff $\lambda_j^5$. They do not themselves prove these choices admissible or state the older-gradient estimate at $j-2$ mentioned in the paragraph. Existence of suitable step data is a further conclusion of Theorem 7.1.

e03-s7-half-length-decay.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_halfLength_: The formal theorem proves both inequalities for every stage once the initial frequency exceeds an absolute threshold. It also proves positivity of each half-length and only assumes the frequency recurrence, greatest-order choice, positive thresholds and logarithmic floor. It does not require the threshold to be nondecreasing or to majorize analytic constants.

e03-s7-step-constant.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_step_consta: For $\mu\ge1$, integer $b\ge1$, $\lambda=\mu^{320b(q_j+1)}$ and any $A\le\mu$, the formal theorem proves $A(\mu^9)^b\le\mu^{10b}\le\lambda^{1/32}$ and also $A(\mu^9)^b\mu\le\lambda^{1/16}$. The choice $A=\mathcal B(q_{j+1})$ gives the displayed chain after the recurrence supplies $A\le\mu$.

e03-s7-base-velocity.TorusEuler.norm_stationaryShear_le: The formal pointwise bound $|U_0(x)|\le2$ holds for all $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and every $|\rho|\le1$, while the construction uses the particular positive tilt $\rho=\varepsilon_1$. Periodicity makes this the stated uniform torus bound.

e03-s7-base-deformations.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobian_: For every $|\rho|\le1$, every label and every $t\in[0,1]$, the formal theorem bounds the forward derivative and inverse derivative at the transported point by $1+4\pi$. The paper uses the same result at its specific positive tilt and $S_0=1$.

r2-s7-base-induction.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The sentence asserts that, for large $N$, the shear $U_0$ of (6.1) satisfies (T1)–(T3) on $[0,S_0]$ with $S_0=1$. The formal conclusions of Theorem 7.1 state that the stage-zero field is the stationary shear at $\rho=\varepsilon_1$, that $S_0=1$, and that (T1)–(T3) hold at every stage $j\ge0$, including $j=0$, for every sufficiently large initial frequency; at $j=0$ this includes smoothness, oddness, zero divergence, the frequency band, $\|U_0\|_\infty\le\lambda_0$, the deformation bounds by $\lambda_0$, the residual bound and the pressure condition. The proof obtains this inside the whole construction rather than as a separate lemma, which is a matter of where the argument sits and does not weaken the conclusion. The first-wave direction identities are not part of this sentence.

e03-s7-parent-interval.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_endpointSla: The scalar theorem proves the strict inequality $S_j<S_{j-1}$ from the half-length decay, $\tau_1\le1/4$, $t_1=0$ and the activation-gap upper bounds. The paper only needs $[0,S_j]\subset[0,S_{j-1}]$ here. Existence of the parent velocity on the larger interval is supplied by the construction.

e03-s7-pressure-sum.TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le: For positive $\lambda_0=N$ and $2\lambda_i\le\lambda_{i+1}$, the formal theorem gives $\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1}\le2/N$ for every $j$, including the empty sum at zero. This is the pressure allowance in (T3), with exactly the stated hypotheses.

r2-s7-parent-coercivity.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The proof supplies the parent condition needed by the endpoint problem using a separately established parent estimate. It does not export $D^2\pi_{j-1}-\nabla R_{j-1}\le(2/N+C\mu^5\lambda^{-3})I$ as its conclusion. The displayed intermediate numerical bound should therefore not be read as a separately stated theorem at this link.

r2-s7-first-wave-input.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: Lemma 6.1 proves the two central estimates and initial strength interval when $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$. Substituting $\lambda=\lambda_1$, $T=S_1$ and $\rho=\varepsilon_1$ supplies that part of the paragraph. The large-frequency shortness and exact coupling values are additional inputs.
r2-s7-first-wave-input.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_coupl: For the first wave with positive frequency and positive initial amplitude along $e_2$, the formal calculation gives $\nu_1(0)=2\pi$ and $\eta_1(0)=2\pi\rho$. Setting $\rho=\varepsilon_1$ gives the last sentence. It does not prove the preceding propagation, strength or endpoint-smallness assertions.

e03-s7-growth-rate.TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds: From $c\mu^{1/4}\le\sigma\le C\mu^{1/4}L_j^2$, $\pi\le\nu\le4\pi$, positive $c,C,\mu$ and $L_j\ge0$, the formal theorem proves $\sqrt{2c\pi}\mu^{1/8}\le r\le\sqrt{8C\pi}\mu^{1/8}L_j$. It supplies explicit constants in the quoted comparison. The strength and coupling estimates are hypotheses.

e03-s7-older-gradient.TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal: For $\mu=\lambda_{j-2}^{320b(q+1)}$, $b\ge1$ and $\lambda_{j-2}\ge1$, the formal theorem assumes bounds $B\le\lambda_{j-2}^9$ and $B_t\le\lambda_{j-2}^{18}$ and concludes $B\le\mu^{1/32}$ and $B_t\le\mu^{1/16}$. It supplies the comparison of scales, not the prior analytic bounds on the actual older gradient.

e03-s7-error-budget.TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu: The formal theorem assumes the physical error bound, the older-gradient and correction bounds, $r\ge c\mu^{1/8}$, $\nu\ge1$, and positive gains. It then gives the displayed expression with explicit coefficient $A(5+c^{-1})$ in place of the unspecified absolute constant. It does not itself prove the error hypothesis or comparison smallness.

r2-s7-comparison-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: For one fixed sufficiently large comparison constant $C_0$, the paper increases the initial frequency $N$ so that every induction step satisfies $C_0\varepsilon_{j-1}\le1$ and $C_0\Theta_j^{C_0}\delta_j\le\varepsilon_{j-1}$ for the later wave $j\ge2$. The formal conditions retain two guarantees. The supplied construction carries one integer $C\ge240$ for which these inequalities hold at every later wave. In addition, for each fixed integer $C_0$, all sufficiently late waves satisfy them. Here $\Theta_j=r_j(S_j-t_j)$, $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$, and $\delta_j$ is the comparison error (2.6) for wave $j$, with suprema over $[t_j,S_j]$. The latter assertion is an eventual statement for each $C_0$, not a replacement for the carried all-stage comparison. Neither clause states the displayed logarithmic estimates. In the exported existence statement, the construction and its carried constant are chosen after $N$; the paper's argument fixes its comparison constant before the large-$N$ choice.
r2-s7-comparison-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The construction theorem assumes Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.5–2.7, 5.8–5.10, 6.1 and B.1 and Propositions 2.8, 5.4 and 5.11. Its proof chooses one comparison constant and a large-frequency threshold, then constructs the sequence with the required comparison at every later wave. The exported conditions also say that, for each fixed integer comparison constant, all sufficiently late waves satisfy the smallness inequalities. They do not state the intermediate estimates in powers of $\log\mu$ quoted here. Thus the link locates the construction argument and its resulting guarantees, rather than a separate statement of those logarithmic inequalities.

e03-s7-ratio-decay.TorusEuler.couplingRatioOfGain_step: For $L_j>0$ and $L_{j+1}\ge640L_j$, the square of the ratio $L_j/L_{j+1}$ is at most $1/32$. Multiplying by $L_j^{-2}$ gives $L_{j+1}^{-2}\le L_j^{-2}/32$. With $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ and $\varepsilon_j=L_{j+1}^{-2}$ this is (7.9).

e03-s7-crossing-half-window.TorusEuler.crossingClock_le_endpointHalf: Assuming $\mu,c,L_j>0$, $L_{j+1}\ge640L_j$, $r\ge c\mu^{1/8}$ and $L_{j+1}\ge2/c$, the theorem concludes $2(\varepsilon\varepsilon_j)^{-1/2}/r\le\tau_j$. It omits the displayed intermediate bound by a constant times $\mu^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^2$ and assumes, rather than constructs, the crossing horizon.

e03-s7-cumulative-log.TorusEuler.firstCoupling_cumulative_log_: For positive crossing couplings, nonnegative ratios decreasing by a factor at least thirty-two, and local logarithmic increments at most twice the ratio, the formal theorem gives the accumulated bound by four times the initial ratio. Setting the initial coupling to $2\pi$ yields the first inequality; comparison with $(\log N)^{-2}$ requires the schedule separately.

e03-s7-uniform-coupling.TorusEuler.firstCoupling_pi_bounds: The formal result assumes initial coupling $2\pi$, positive couplings, ratios decreasing by at least a factor thirty-two, local logarithmic increments bounded by twice the ratio, and initial smallness $4\varepsilon_1\le\log2$. It concludes $\pi\le\nu_j(t_{j+1})\le4\pi$. The paper obtains that explicit smallness by choosing $N$ large.

e03-s7-switch-residual.TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w: The theorem fixes a cutoff-dependent constant before the parameters. If $r,\lambda_{j+1}>0$, $|\gamma|\le e^{3-4\log\lambda_{j+1}}$ on the switching interval and $Cre^3\le\mu$, it proves $|\widetilde\chi^{\prime}\gamma|\le\mu\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ for all real times. These are exactly the two inputs checked in the preceding sentence.

r2-s7-expansion-step.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The proof of Theorem 7.1 supplies the parent conditions and numerical estimates before invoking the assumed Section 5 results. Its statement asserts the resulting common construction and step data, rather than separately asserting the displayed bound for $C_{\rm step}$. The scalar step-constant theorem gives that inequality directly.

e03-s7-depth-residual-identity.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_residual_ex: For $\lambda>0$, integer $K_{j+1}$ and $P=6K_{j+1}$, the formal identity $\lambda^{-2P/3}=(\lambda^{K_{j+1}})^{-4}$ is precisely the displayed chain after simplifying $-2P/3=-4K_{j+1}$ and setting $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda^{K_{j+1}}$. Omitting an algebraically identical intermediate expression does not weaken the conclusion.

e03-s7-residual-power.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_residual_bu: The theorem handles the second inequality in (7.11). Substituting $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda^{320b(q_{j+1}+1)}$ for $\lambda\ge2$ and integer $b\ge1$ absorbs $2\lambda^{2+1/16}$ into $\lambda_{j+1}^{1/2}$. The bound of the actual residual by $2\lambda^{2+1/16}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ is the analytic input from the expansion.

e03-s7-parent-full-order.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_fullOrder_p: If $\mu\ge1$, integer $b\ge1$, $C_P\le\mu$ and $\lambda=\mu^{320b(q_j+1)}$, the formal theorem proves $C_P\mu^{5(P+1)+1}\le\lambda^{P+2}$. It does not contain the actual parent velocity or the preceding Bernstein estimate for its norm.

e03-s7-wave-coefficient-cost.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_fullOrder_w: For $\mu\ge1$, $C_{P,P}\le\mu$, integers $b\ge1$ and $P,q_j\ge0$, the theorem gives $C_{P,P}(\mu^9)^{b(P+2)}\le(\mu^{320b(q_j+1)})^{(P+2)/32}$. These are exactly the paper's coefficient and frequency after $\mathsf D=\mu^9$ and $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$ are substituted.

e03-s7-cutoff-tail.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_tail_absorp: With $\mu\ge2$, integer $b\ge1$, $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$, $P=6K_{j+1}$ and $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda^{K_{j+1}}$, the theorem proves $9\mu\lambda^{5(2-P)+4(P+1)}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}$. It does not estimate the actual Fourier tail $\varepsilon_\Lambda$ or state each intermediate inequality in the display. Here $2-P$ is real subtraction, not subtraction truncated at zero.

r2-s7-new-truncation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: The step condition requires $U_j=S_{\lambda_j^5}(U_{j-1}+W^{\natural})$ on $[0,S_j]$, with the chosen Fourier symbol and the zero-mean pressure of the truncated field. This is precisely the displayed choice, as a required identity for proposed step data.
r2-s7-new-truncation.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The numbered theorem supplies expansion data at every $j\ge1$ and requires their truncation to equal $U_j$. Thus it proves that the actual common construction has the identity $U_j=S_{\Lambda_j}V$, with $\Lambda_j=\lambda_j^5$, rather than merely postulating that identity.

r2-s7-flow-input.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: Assuming the preceding results, including Lemma 5.10, this proof builds the common sequence with flow and inverse-flow derivatives bounded by $\lambda_j$. Its statement does not retain the intermediate bound $C_{\rm step}\lambda_j^{1/4}$ or the separate perturbation test for the Fourier tail. That lemma states that if $v$ is smooth and divergence free with derivatives through order two bounded by $\lambda^{-5/2}$, the flow $Y$ of $V+v$ satisfies $\sup|(D_aY)^{\pm1}|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$.

r2-s7-localized-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal common-sequence condition requires support within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of the integer lattice, the paper's torus ball. It does not state the preceding label-support bound, transport by the flow, or the intermediate inequalities $2\mathsf D\ell_*\le2\mathsf D^{-2}\le\mu^{-1}$. This condition alone also leaves the identification with the finite expansion to separate step data.

e03-s7-low-order-mean-cost.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_lowOrder_me: For $m\le q_j$, $\mu\ge1$, integer $b\ge1$ and $C_{m,P}\le\mu$, the formal theorem proves $C_{m,P}(\mu^9)^{b(m+2)}\le\lambda^{1/16}$. It does not state the additional intermediate bound by $\mu^{10b(m+2)}$ appearing in the paper's chain. The theorem is numerical and does not itself bound the mean field.

e03-s7-velocity-increment.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_child_veloc: The formal theorem assumes the decomposition into parent, oscillation, mean and tail and the stated spatial Hölder bounds for mean and tail, then proves the remaining increment has norm at most $\lambda^{-1}$ at a fixed time. The reference to all of (7.4) also includes the oscillation bound and continuity in time, neither of which is a conclusion of this theorem.

e03-s7-new-velocity.TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun: Under $\mu\ge2$, $\lambda\ge2\mu$, parent bound $\mu$, oscillation bound $\lambda^{-1}$, and remaining $C^{0,1/2}$ increment bound $\lambda^{-1}$, the theorem concludes the pointwise bound $|U_j(x)|\le\lambda$. It uses $\mu+2\lambda^{-1}$ in the proof but does not state that intermediate bound or a time-continuity assertion.

e03-s7-central-error.TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_: For $\lambda\ge2^{12}$ and $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda$, the formal theorem proves $\lambda^{-1/3}+\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}\le\lambda^{-1/4}$. It has no central error field among its data. The preceding bound for $|E_{c,j}|$ must be supplied by the expansion and truncation estimates.

r2-s7-completion.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The assembly proof concludes the central splitting, activation and crossing bounds of the common sequence, assuming the cited preceding results. It does not export each calculation in this completion paragraph separately. Its formal central covector is not explicitly identified with the transported covector of the localized step, so the paper's full object identification is still missing.

e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The selected sequence has its first two activation times at zero. After the second launch, all later launches are strictly separated. The clock bound and the convergence of those times are additional conclusions of the same construction.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `activation_strict` starts with the comparison of index $2$ with index $3$. The separate initial field sets both indices $1$ and $2$ to zero. Thus the strict part of the clock begins exactly where the passage places it.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The field `times_increase` takes the hypothesis $2\le j$ before comparing successive activation times. It can therefore be used to order the intervals for the later amplifying waves without asserting a positive gap between the first two.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement asks for a construction with this order of the launch times, together with a separate upper bound on each gap. Strict increase from stage two gives a positive length for each of those activation intervals.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The theorem produces the strictly increasing part of the clock for the wave sequence it selects. Wave one is present when wave two starts at zero, after which each crossing gives a later launch of the following wave.

e03-s7-terminal-room.TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge: For nonnegative initial time, positive half-lengths with $4\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j$, gaps between zero and $\tau_j$, and no eventually constant tail, the formal theorem gives $0<T_\infty-t_j\le4\tau_j/3$ and $T_\infty<t_j+2\tau_j$. It does not state the comparison with the infinite sum as a separate conclusion, although that estimate is used in its proof.

e03-s7-all-endpoints.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_commonLifet: Assuming the positive half-lengths, their factor-four decay, activation-gap bounds, strict later increase, the prescribed final times and a sufficiently large initial frequency, the formal theorem supplies $T_\infty<S_j$ for every stage, including $j=0$. This is exactly the endpoint conclusion. The hypotheses are the scalar properties already checked in the induction.

r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8: This condition asks for numerical parameters, an approximate sequence satisfying the smoothness, residual, support, increment and central-wave estimates of Theorem 7.1, and a common time $T_\infty>0$. It requires $t_j\to T_\infty$ and $T_\infty<S_j$ for every stage, so all stages exist on $[0,T_\infty]$. This supplies the quoted setting only. It contains no limiting velocity or convergence assertion. Existence is proved by the other linked declarations.
r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting: The formal statement proves existence of one approximate sequence with the smoothness, residual, support, increment and central-wave estimates of Theorem 7.1, and a finite $T_\infty>0$ with $t_j\to T_\infty<S_j$ for every stage. Thus $[0,T_\infty]$ is a common interval as quoted. It does not yet introduce a velocity limit or assert convergence on that interval.
r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set: Assuming Theorem 7.1, the formal statement selects parameters and an approximate sequence with its residual, support, increment and central-wave estimates. It supplies a finite $T_\infty>0$ with activation times tending to $T_\infty$ and $T_\infty<S_j$ for every stage. This proves the quoted choice of a common interval. Uniform convergence to a continuous velocity is a separate conclusion, absent from this declaration.

r3c8-s8-increment-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: The paper gives $\|U_j-U_{j-1}\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$. The formal theorem concludes a continuous uniform limit on $[0,T_\infty]$ and its agreement with the Euler limit before $T_\infty$. Its proof establishes the pointwise increment estimate uniformly in time and space, but that estimate is not a separately quantified conclusion of the linked declaration.

e03-s8-summable.TorusEuler.reciprocal_inductive_frequenc: The paper uses convergence of the reciprocal-frequency sum for its chosen schedule. For any real sequence with $\lambda_0\ge2$ and $\lambda_{n+1}\ge\lambda_n^2$, the formal theorem proves convergence of every tail and $\sum_{k\ge0}\lambda_{j+k}^{-1}\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$. Thus it supplies an explicit uniform tail bound in addition to the stated summability.

e03-s8-uniform-limit.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: The paper derives a continuous uniform limit directly from the increment bound at the beginning of Section 8. The formal theorem states that limit and also identifies it with the smooth Euler solution for $t<T_\infty$, but takes the conclusions of Proposition 8.1 as an additional input for that identification. The continuous-limit assertion itself is present. The ordering and hypotheses of this declaration differ from the opening argument.

r3c8-s8-derivative-strategy.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The paper describes derivative convergence using vanishing before activation and shrinking support. The formal condition supplies $O_j=0$ on $[0,t_j]$ for $j\ge2$ and support within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of the integer lattice on each stage interval. These are the two inputs. Shrinking of that radius and convergence of derivatives still use the schedule and increment estimates; they are not the conclusion of this linked condition.

e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: For compatible stages with $T>0$, $T\le S_j$, $\lambda_0\ge2$ and $t_j\to T$, the formal theorem gives the stated initial-data convergence and also constructs a smooth odd Euler limit, continuous velocity convergence through $T$, convergence on every earlier interval, and comparison with any maximal solution of finite lifespan. Its conclusion contains substantially more than the quoted initial-data sentence.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement: The formal condition requires the quoted initial convergence to a smooth odd divergence-free datum and additionally requires smooth Euler evolution, a continuous closed-interval velocity limit, earlier-interval convergence and agreement with every maximal solution of finite lifespan. This row describes required properties. The adjoining theorem establishes their existence.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: Under the common-construction hypothesis of Theorem 7.1, the formal statement asserts the quoted convergence and also existence of a smooth odd Euler solution, convergence on every earlier interval and conditional agreement with every maximal solution of finite lifespan. The printed sentence states only the initial-data part.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: For the construction of Theorem 7.1, the formal theorem proves the quoted initial-data convergence together with smooth odd Euler evolution, all earlier-interval convergence and conditional agreement with maximal solutions of finite lifespan. Thus its conclusion extends beyond this initial-data sentence.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The formal condition requires the quoted initial-data convergence, smooth odd divergence-free initial data, smooth Euler evolution, earlier-interval convergence and a conditional comparison with maximal solutions of finite lifespan. It specifies all these properties together rather than only the quoted convergence. Existence is proved separately.

e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement: The formal condition requires smoothness of $u(0)$, periodicity through the Euler condition, oddness and zero divergence, together with initial and later convergence, a closed-interval continuous velocity limit and maximal-solution agreement. The paper’s sentence states only smoothness of the limiting datum. This condition does not itself prove existence.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: The formal theorem constructs the smooth initial datum together with the Euler solution, oddness, divergence freedom, both initial and earlier-interval convergence, a continuous terminal velocity and comparison with maximal solutions of finite lifespan. Smoothness of the datum is one part of this larger conclusion.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The formal statement includes existence of the smooth datum and smooth odd Euler evolution, convergence in all spatial Hölder orders before accumulation and conditional maximal-solution agreement. The quoted sentence asserts only smoothness of the already constructed datum.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: The formal theorem proves smoothness of the limiting datum together with the preterminal Euler solution, all earlier-interval convergence and conditional comparison with maximal solutions of finite lifespan. These are additional conclusions beyond the quoted sentence.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The formal condition includes a smooth initial datum, oddness, zero divergence, smooth periodic Euler evolution, earlier-interval convergence and conditional maximal-solution agreement. The quoted sentence states only initial smoothness. The condition specifies the properties; a separate theorem proves they are attained.

r3c8-s8-maximal-solution-interface.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The paper starts with the maximal solution supplied by general existence theory, whose lifespan might still be infinite at this stage. The formal statement instead constructs a smooth Euler solution on $[0,T_\infty)$ and compares it with each maximal solution whose lifespan is a finite real number. It does not assert existence of that general maximal solution. Maximality of the constructed solution is established later.
r3c8-s8-maximal-solution-interface.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The paper takes an existing maximal smooth Euler solution from $u_0$. The formal condition requires the constructed preterminal Euler solution and an implication concerning every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same datum. It neither supplies that other solution nor permits an infinite value for its lifespan. This is a conditional comparison, not a maximal-existence theorem.

e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: The formal theorem constructs a smooth odd solution on $[0,T_\infty)$ and gives the stated earlier-interval convergence. It compares its lifespan only conditionally with maximal solutions of finite lifespan from the same initial datum, instead of starting with the general maximal solution used in the paper.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: The formal theorem assumes compatible stages and central waves above a separately chosen initial-frequency threshold. It gives the stated convergence, but also finite maximality, central blow-up, both infinite integrals and terminal limits away from the origin. Both its explicit input and its conclusion exceed the scope of this sentence. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The formal statement gives a smooth odd preterminal Euler solution and the displayed convergence in each spatial Hölder order. The lifespan comparison is an implication for any maximal solution with a finite real lifespan, rather than an assertion about a general maximal solution already supplied by local existence theory.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: The formal theorem proves the displayed convergence, smoothness and oddness for its constructed solution. It asserts the lower lifespan bound only conditionally for each maximal solution of finite lifespan having the same initial data. It does not prove general maximal-solution existence.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The formal condition includes the stated earlier-interval convergence, smoothness and oddness. It requires the lower lifespan bound and velocity agreement for maximal solutions of finite lifespan, conditional on their existence. The paper uses the maximal solution from general theory, before finiteness of its lifespan has been proved.

r2-s8-orders-and-times.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The paper chooses an index meeting both $T\le t_{j_0}$ and $m\le q_{j_0}$. The formal theorem concludes existence and convergence of the Euler limit. The supplied proof passes convergence of activation times and growth of derivative orders to a limit theorem, but does not export this simultaneous choice of $j_0$ as its conclusion. This link locates the argument, not a matching index-selection statement.

e03-s8-late-vanishing.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: The paper uses the particular index $j_0$ chosen in the preceding sentence. The formal theorem proves that all sufficiently late oscillations vanish on $[0,T]$, but does not identify its eventual index with that chosen $j_0$.

e03-s8-tail-estimate.TorusEuler.reciprocal_inductive_frequenc: The paper first bounds the velocity difference by a sum of reciprocal frequencies. The formal lemma proves summability and the tail bound $2\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$; the first inequality also needs the increment estimates and vanishing of the oscillations.

r2-s8-nonlinear-limit.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The paper gives a residual-integral estimate, convergence of the projected nonlinear term and joint smoothness of the limit. The formal theorem constructs the smooth Euler limit assuming Lemma 1.3 and (5.59), and its proof passes through the same steps: a residual tending to zero by (T2), uniform convergence of the projected quadratic term from the product estimate (5.59), and the limit of the integrated stage equation. Those intermediate estimates are not separate conclusions of the formal statement, so the comparison is different.

e03-s8-uniqueness.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.velocity_eq_o: Let $u,p$ and $v,q$ be smooth periodic incompressible Euler solutions, with mean-zero pressures, on $[0,T_1)$ and $[0,T_2)$ for finite $T_1,T_2>0$. If $u(0)=v(0)$, the formal statement proves $u(t,x)=v(t,x)$ for every $x$ and $0\le t<\min(T_1,T_2)$. This is the uniqueness used to identify the two velocities on their common interval. Neither maximality nor equality of the lifespans is assumed or concluded.
e03-s8-uniqueness.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The paper invokes uniqueness wherever the limit and the maximal solution coexist. The formal proposition concludes comparison with maximal solutions of finite lifespan and uses the separate uniqueness theorem in its proof. That conclusion does not by itself state general uniqueness for every pair of smooth Euler solutions. The first linked theorem does.

r5-term-lifespan-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The formal theorem constructs the solution on $[0,T_\infty)$ and uses velocity uniqueness to show that any maximal solution of finite lifespan from its initial data has lifespan at least $T_\infty$. The paper invokes the maximal solution from general theory, whose lifespan has not yet been proved finite. The formal comparison is conditional on such a finite-lifespan maximal solution being supplied.

e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: The assembly theorem takes compatible approximate stages, their central waves, and an initial frequency above a fixed threshold. It produces one limit $u$ and one accumulation time $T$, and gives `PaperTerminalVelocityCurl T u` for that same limit. Its first clause is the bound in the passage, with one constant for every $0\le t<T$.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl: In `PaperTerminalVelocityCurl T u`, the first clause chooses one finite constant $C$ before quantifying over all $0\le t<T$. It bounds $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}$, the essential supremum of the speed on the unit torus. The second clause uses the same $u$ and $T$ and requires $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$. The definition specifies both properties for a given velocity.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The statement takes the construction from Theorem 7.1 and the Euler limit from Proposition 8.1 as inputs. In `Proposition82Conclusions`, `bounded_velocity` asks for one constant over the whole interval $[0,T_\infty)$. Two further clauses concern the same $u$: its central curl diverges, and on all sufficiently late intervals it exceeds $c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2: The proof uses the uniform limit of the approximate velocities on the closed slab through $T_\infty$. The continuous limit is bounded there and agrees with the Euler velocity before $T_\infty$, so a single speed bound works for the whole half-open lifespan. The theorem supplies this bound and the two central-curl clauses of `Proposition82Conclusions` for the same Euler limit.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion: The field `bounded_velocity` fixes the constant $M$ before choosing $t\in[0,T_\infty)$, so the essential supremum of $|u(t,x)|$ has a uniform bound. The two other fields require central curl divergence and one lower bound with fixed constants on all sufficiently late activation intervals. Proposition 8.2 establishes the three fields for the Euler limit.

e03-s8-central-curl.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: The theorem produces $T$ and an Euler limit $u$ from compatible stages and central waves with sufficiently large starting frequency. Its output `PaperTerminalVelocityCurl T u` includes divergence of $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|$ along the whole approach to the same $T$ that the activation times approach. It also bounds the speed of $u$ and proves its maximal lifespan and off-origin limits.
e03-s8-central-curl.TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl: The second clause of `PaperTerminalVelocityCurl T u` means that for any prescribed level, the norm of $\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)$ exceeds it for all $t$ sufficiently close to $T$ from below. The first clause imposes one uniform bound on the speed of that same $u$ for $0\le t<T$. This definition specifies the two properties of a supplied field.
e03-s8-central-curl.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: For the construction in Theorem 7.1 and the limit in Proposition 8.1, `central_curl` gives the full left-hand limit. The stronger quantitative field `curl_lower` fixes $c>0$ and $C$ before choosing the late activation interval and time, and bounds $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|$ below by $c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. The statement also bounds the speed of $u$.
e03-s8-central-curl.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2: The proof carries the lower bound from $U_j$ to the limit $u$ on each late activation interval. The curl of the tail is uniformly small there because the subsequent oscillations vanish and the first derivatives of the remaining corrections are summable. The intervals cover a terminal segment, so the bound implies divergence throughout the approach to $T_\infty$.
e03-s8-central-curl.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion: The `central_curl` field expresses the full limit from below. The same record contains `bounded_velocity` and the quantitative field `curl_lower`, where one pair of constants works for all sufficiently late $j$ and every $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Those are requirements on the supplied Euler limit.

e03-s8-compact-bound.TorusEuler.terminalVelocityBound_of_exte: The paper has already constructed the continuous $w$ and identifies it with $u$, then deduces boundedness. This formal theorem assumes continuity on the closed time interval and centred cell and assumes agreement there before the terminal time. It concludes the velocity bound but does not prove that agreement.
e03-s8-compact-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: The formal theorem supplies a continuous closed-interval uniform limit $w$ and agreement $u(t)=w(t)$ for $t<T_\infty$, from the common-construction and Proposition 8.1 hypotheses. Boundedness on the torus is the separate compactness conclusion supplied by the first linked theorem.

e03-s8-rank-one.TorusEuler.coordinateCurl_rankOne: For any $\mathbf a,\kappa\in\mathbb R^3$, let $D(v)=(\kappa\cdot v)\mathbf a$, the derivative-matrix convention for $\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$. Its coordinate curl is $\kappa\times\mathbf a$, with the usual orientation. This exactly gives the vorticity contribution in the quotation. No nonzero-vector or orthogonality assumption is needed. This is an algebraic identity, applied when $D$ is a term of a velocity gradient.

e03-s8-projection-cancel.TorusEuler.inner_normalize_cross3_left: For arbitrary $\kappa,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal statement gives $(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot(\kappa\times\mathbf a)=0$. At $\kappa=0$ the normalized vector is defined as zero. It is a unit vector only when $\kappa\ne0$. Consequently the vorticity $\widetilde\chi_j\kappa_j\times\mathbf a_j$ of the leading rank-one term has zero projection along $\kappa_j$, for every real cutoff value. This proves the quoted cancellation and gives no estimate for the preceding wave.

r2-s8-geometry-before-projection.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: Writing $\kappa/\lambda=\zeta_1E_1+(\zeta_2/S)E_2+\zeta_3E_3$ in the preceding frame, the formal theorem gives $|\zeta_1|\le T^2$, $|\zeta_2|\le T$ and $|\zeta_3-1|\le1/2$ throughout a normalized window of length $T$. It assumes the nonzero initial scale, $T\ge2$, $C_0\ge240$, the time-change image stays in the prescribed interval, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. These whole-window bounds do not state the paper’s covector length bound $C(1+\tau^2)$ at each normalized time $\tau$; the scheduled window bound is another input. The physical error size is the paper’s $\delta$ in (2.6), with suprema over the interval on which the data are given.
r2-s8-geometry-before-projection.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal condition supplies a constant bounding the normalized comparison-window length by $CL_{j+1}^4$. It does not itself contain the covector component and length estimates in the first part of the sentence. The geometry and the window estimate are separate inputs.

e03-s8-retained-strength.TorusEuler.preceding_strength_retained_o: The paper says the preceding wave retains its strength and then estimates the change of its logarithm. Assuming $\mu\ge1$, an interval of length at most $\mu^{-1/16}$, a trace-free gradient bounded by $\mu^{1/32}$, and nonzero transverse wave solutions, the formal theorem gives the explicit bound $\sigma(t)\ge e^{-1}\sigma(t_j)$ throughout that interval. This quantifies retention. It does not assert constant strength.

e03-s8-curl-lower.TorusEuler.norm_curlOfDerivative_ge_of_t: The paper asserts (8.2) for the actual approximation $U_j$. The formal theorem assumes two rank-one gradient decompositions, a lower bound $b$ for the preceding wave’s signed projection, and bounds $M,e_p,e$ for the older gradient and errors. It concludes $|\operatorname{curl}D_{\rm new}|\ge b-C(M+e_p+e)$. Obtaining (8.2) still requires $b\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}$ and the induction bounds for $M,e_p,e$; these powers are not conclusions of this declaration.

r2-s8-curl-tail.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82: The paper gives a bound for $\operatorname{curl}(u-U_j)$ by the reciprocal-frequency tail throughout the activation interval. The formal theorem concludes bounded velocity, full central blow-up and a lower bound for $|\operatorname{curl}u|$. Its proof uses derivative convergence, but the displayed tail inequality is not one of its conclusions. This is a proof-location link rather than a matching statement of the error bound.

e03-s8-full-limit.TorusEuler.terminalCurl_tendsto_atTop_of: The formal theorem assumes $t_j\to T_\infty$ from below, interval lower bounds $b_j\to\infty$ for $|\operatorname{curl}U_j|$, and interval bounds $e_j\to0$ for the gradient difference between $u$ and $U_j$. It then proves the full one-sided central-vorticity limit. The paper also derives these interval and tail estimates from the construction. Those derivations are hypotheses, not conclusions, of this transfer theorem.

e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: Under compatible stages and central waves above its initial-frequency threshold, the formal theorem identifies the common activation limit with a positive maximal lifespan and proves both infinite integrals. It also gives all other Section 8 limits and bounds. This is a larger construction-specific theorem with its own input, not only the quoted corollary. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.
e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals.TorusEuler.PaperTerminalTime: The formal condition requires maximal Euler evolution at a prescribed positive finite $T$ and both infinite integrals. It does not itself identify $T$ with $T_\infty$, the limit of the activation times. That identification is part of the theorem that supplies these properties for the common construction. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.
e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3: The conclusion gives exactly the positive maximal time and both divergent integrals, including agreement of the time for other maximal solutions of finite lifespan. The formal implication takes the strengthened Proposition 8.2 conclusions as input, including the quantitative lower bound on late activation intervals. The printed corollary invokes the general continuation criterion instead. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.
e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals.TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3: The theorem gives the stated maximal time and both divergent integrals for the common construction. Its explicit hypotheses include the quantitative interval lower bound exported by the formal Proposition 8.2, beyond that proposition’s printed qualitative statement. Its proof uses that bound with crossing durations rather than the general continuation criterion. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.
e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals.TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions: The formal condition requires a positive finite maximal lifespan $T$, both infinite integrals and the same lifespan for any other maximal solution of finite lifespan from the data. It does not itself identify $T$ as the activation limit $T_\infty$ or prove existence. The corollary supplies this condition at that particular time. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.

e03-s8-maximality-proof.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.isMaximal_of_: The paper combines impossibility of continuation beyond $T_\infty$ with the earlier inequality $T_*\ge T_\infty$. The formal theorem proves noncontinuation for a smooth Euler solution whose central vorticity tends to infinity. Identifying its time with the lifespan of another maximal solution also requires the existence and agreement information from Proposition 8.1.
e03-s8-maximality-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3: The formal theorem concludes maximality, equality of finite maximal lifespans and both infinite integrals. Its proof uses this central-vorticity contradiction for maximality, but its full statement also assumes the quantitative interval bound from the strengthened Proposition 8.2. The quoted passage concerns only the time-identification argument. The two integrals are $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_{[0,T_\infty)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$, with essential suprema on the unit torus.

e03-s8-bkm-boundary.TorusEuler.theorem11_of_continuation_and: This theorem accepts the continuation implication as a hypothesis. If a finite vorticity integral would extend the given smooth solution past $T$, central curl divergence rules out that extension. The argument then gives the infinite vorticity integral and uses the curl-to-gradient bound for the other integral. The continuation implication is the step supplied by Beale–Kato–Majda in the paper.
e03-s8-bkm-boundary.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3: The formal proof derives divergence directly by summing the quantitative curl lower bounds from Proposition 8.2 over activation intervals whose lengths are controlled by the construction. The paper invokes the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion after proving maximality. Both routes give divergence of the curl integral for the same terminal Euler solution.

e03-s8-gradient-integral.TorusEuler.gradientIntegral_eq_top_of_cu: For any field $u$ and real $T$, if the nonnegative Lebesgue integral $\int_{[0,T)}\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ is infinite, then so is $\int_{[0,T)}\|D_xu(t)\|_\infty\,dt$. The norms are essential suprema over the centred unit cell, and $D_xu$ uses the Euclidean operator norm. The deduction uses a fixed linear curl bound. It requires no Euler equation or continuation theorem. For the smooth periodic solution in the paper these are the ordinary gradient and vorticity norms.

e03-s8-curl-gradient.TorusEuler.torusLInf_curl_le: For any $v:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, the formal statement gives $\|\operatorname{curl}v\|_\infty\le C\|D_xv\|_\infty$, where $C$ is the operator norm of the fixed linear map from a derivative matrix to its coordinate curl. Both essential suprema use the centred unit cell. The matrix norm is the Euclidean operator norm. At points without a spatial derivative the derivative expression is assigned zero. For the smooth periodic velocity of the paper, no default value is used and this is precisely the quoted inequality.

e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: For compatible stages and their central waves starting above a fixed frequency threshold, the assembly theorem gives one Euler limit $u$ and one time $T$. The conclusion `PaperTerminalOffOrigin T u` supplies both families of spatial limits away from the origin, with $u$ and $\partial_tu$ evaluated at that same endpoint from below.
e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.PaperTerminalOffOrigin: `PaperTerminalOffOrigin T u` applies the one-field condition `HasOffOriginLimits` to $u$ and to `timeDerivative T u`. In both applications the limit uses $t\uparrow T$, and for each compact set avoiding the lattice it includes uniform convergence of all spatial derivatives up to the given order.
e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.HasOffOriginLimits: The input to `HasOffOriginLimits` is one field $f$. For each compact $K$ disjoint from $\mathbb Z^3$ and each $m$, it requires a $C^m$ field on an open neighborhood of $K$ whose derivatives through order $m$ are the uniform limits on $K$. Proposition 8.4 uses this one-field condition once for $u$ and again for $\partial_tu$.
e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The statement starts with the construction in Theorem 7.1 and its Euler limit in Proposition 8.1. It concludes `Proposition84Conclusions T u`, so every compact set away from the origin has both spatial limits at each order $m$. The time derivative uses the interval where $u$ solves Euler.
e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4: The proof uses shrinking oscillation supports to obtain the spatial limits of $u$. For $\partial_tu$ it splits the nonlinear term with a cutoff near the chosen compact set. The near term uses spatial Hölder convergence and the far pressure kernel is smooth across the positive gap to the compact set.
e03-s8-off-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion: The fields `velocity` and `time_derivative` both use `HasOffOriginLimits` at the same time $T$. The first applies it to $u$ and the second to $\partial_tu$, with each spatial $C^m$ limit taken locally away from the integer lattice, the lifts of the torus origin.

r5-term-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The paper uses the support bound on the common interval $[0,T_\infty]$. The formal condition imposes it on the whole stage interval $[0,S_j]$, with $T_\infty<S_j$. On the periodic lift, every nonzero value of $O_j$ must lie within $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of some integer lattice point. This is the torus ball stated in the paper, with a longer time interval.

e03-s8-shrinking-support.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: The paper states that the enclosing support balls eventually miss $K$. The formal theorem concludes the consequence actually needed: all late oscillations vanish on an open neighborhood of $K$, uniformly in time. It does not state disjointness of the balls themselves.
e03-s8-shrinking-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o: The paper uses eventual disjointness of the support balls from $K$. The formal proof derives local terminal limits from shrinking support radii and increment bounds, without stating that geometric disjointness as its conclusion.

r2-s8-velocity-trace.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o: The paper identifies the local spatial limit with the value $w(T_\infty)$ of the closed-interval velocity limit and explains summability of the increments. The formal theorem concludes local $C^m$ limits for both $u$ and its time derivative. Its proof obtains and uses the continuous field $w$, but neither the summability assertion nor that named identification is retained in the theorem’s conclusion.

e03-s8-cutoff.TorusEuler.exists_periodic_offOrigin_cut: For compact $K$ avoiding the torus origin, the formal theorem constructs the stated cutoff and also requires period-one spatial dependence, $0\le\chi\le1$, and closed support avoiding every integer lattice point. It gives the separation $x-y\notin\mathbb Z^3$ for $x\in K$ and $y$ in the closed support of $1-\chi$. These additional conclusions justify using a smooth far pressure kernel on the torus.

e03-s8-far-kernel.TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe: The paper bounds the localized Leray-divergence term in $C^m(K)$. For separated compact source and observation sets, the formal theorem bounds each spatial derivative of the difference of two far pressure gradients by a constant times the $L^1$ difference of the source tensors. Identifying this real pressure gradient with the displayed projected term, and combining derivative orders into $C^m(K)$, require adjoining results. The linked estimate alone is not the displayed operator identity.

r2-s8-time-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o: The paper proves uniform convergence of the velocity tensors, deduces their $L^1$ convergence, and applies the separated pressure estimate. The formal theorem concludes the two local spatial limits for $u$ and $\partial_tu$. The supplied proof passes global velocity convergence and local derivative limits to a pressure-limit theorem. The particular tensor and $L^1$ assertions are not exported conclusions of this declaration.

r2-s8-main-assembly.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of: Assume the common approximate sequence selected in Section 8 and the formal versions of Propositions 8.1, 8.2, 8.4 and Corollary 8.3. The formal statement then proves existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data and an odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, $0<T_*<\infty$, with bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and infinite time integrals of both gradient and vorticity supremum norms. On every compact set off the origin, $u$ and $\partial_tu$ have limits with all spatial derivatives. Every maximal solution of finite real lifespan from those data has the same lifespan and velocity before it. This is the assembly asserted by the paper. Its inputs remain hypotheses of this particular theorem and are established separately.

e03-appa-time-norm.TorusEuler.endpointClosedTimeNorm: The formal expression takes the supremum of a chosen norm over $[0,T]$. Taking $T=1$ and choosing the underlying spatial norm to be $C^{k,1/2}$ gives the displayed notation. Its ordinary finite-supremum interpretation requires boundedness; continuous curves on the compact interval have that property in the applications here.

e03-r2-appa-dimensional-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: In spatial dimension three, the formal statement chooses one $C\ge0$ and one nonnegative integer $p$ before the coefficient curves, coercivity constants, coefficient bounds and source. These same constants govern $\|z_t\|_0\le CQ^p\|L\|_0$ for every admissible endpoint problem on $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$. This is the asserted independence from the data. The statement is specialized to dimension three. It does not quantify over the dimension.
e03-r2-appa-dimensional-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: In dimension three, the formal statement chooses one $C\ge0$ and one nonnegative integer $p$ before $B$, its positive coercivity constant, its Lipschitz bound and the datum. The same pair works for both $H=\mathbb R^3$, $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$, and $H=L^2(0,1;\mathbb R^3)$, $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ subtracts the time average. Thus the inverse bounds have the data independence claimed in the sentence. The dimension is fixed, rather than quantified over.

e03-r2-appa-symmetry.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: At every $t\in[0,1]$ and $a\in\mathbb T^3$, the formal numbered statement requires $K(t,a)^T=K(t,a)$ and $\Omega(t,a)^T=-\Omega(t,a)$. These are exactly the two symmetry hypotheses in the selected phrase. They are retained even though the underlying general endpoint inverse does not need separate symmetry hypotheses once its quadratic energy inequality is assumed.

e03-appa-coefficient-regularity.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC1Bound: The paper requires $K,\Omega\in C([0,1];C^{1,1/2})$. The formal coefficient condition requires only continuity in $C^{0,1/2}$, differentiability of each periodic spatial lift, and uniform bounds on the coefficient and its first spatial derivative. It does not require the first derivative to vary continuously in a Hölder norm. Thus this formal hypothesis is weaker. The full inverse theorem using it has correspondingly broader scope.
e03-appa-coefficient-regularity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: The paper's displayed regularity hypothesis is continuity in time in $C^{1,1/2}$. The formal theorem assumes continuity in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatial differentiability, and uniform value and first derivative bounds instead. Symmetry, positive ellipticity and the energy inequality remain separate hypotheses. The weaker coefficient regularity enlarges the class for which the theorem gives the same endpoint conclusion.

e03-appa-primitive.TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive: For a function $v:\mathbb R\to E$ into a real normed space, define $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv(s)\,ds$ using the oriented vector-valued integral. Thus negative $t$ reverses the integration direction, and $Jv(0)=0$. The integral expression is assigned zero when the integrand is not integrable. The integral in a noncomplete target is also assigned zero. These defaults do not assert differentiability or recover a displacement. On a positive finite interval, an $L^2$ velocity with values in a real Hilbert space has an absolutely continuous primitive with derivative $v$ almost everywhere, and zero time mean gives $Jv(T)=0$. The endpoint construction uses continuous curves in complete function spaces, so its integrals have their ordinary meaning. The definition itself imposes none of that regularity. On the normalized interval $[0,1]$ with the paper's integrable input, the defining formula is exactly the displayed one.

e03-appa-ellipticity-and-energy.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: The two selected inequalities are assumptions of this theorem, not estimates it derives from arbitrary coefficients. The energy tests use zero-mean $L^2$ velocities $v$ and their primitives $z=Jv$, giving precisely the stated $H^1_0$ class.
e03-appa-ellipticity-and-energy.TorusEuler.EndpointSobolevEnergyBound: The display includes both pointwise ellipticity and the displacement energy bound. This formal condition records only the latter, with $z$ represented as the primitive of a zero-mean $L^2$ velocity; ellipticity is imposed separately.
e03-appa-ellipticity-and-energy.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: In particular the two inequalities in the display are exactly its ellipticity and displacement-energy assumptions. The formal tests represent $z$ by $Jv$ with $\int_0^1v=0$.

e03-r2-appa-size-parameter.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: The paper uses $Q_{\mathrm{paper}}=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+\|K\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+\|\Omega\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}$. The formal statement instead uses $Q_{\mathrm{formal}}=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$, where the four nonnegative bounds control values and first spatial derivatives uniformly on $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$. Under the paper's hypotheses these bounds can be chosen so that $Q_{\mathrm{formal}}\le C Q_{\mathrm{paper}}$. No reverse control is asserted: first derivative suprema do not control their half-Hölder seminorms, and the supplied bounds may be arbitrarily large. The formulas differ, while the one-way comparison suffices for the paper's estimate.

e03-appa-forcing-continuity.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: The source $L$ is a curve on $[0,1]$ in vector-valued $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$, continuous in that spatial norm. The formal statement requires exactly this time continuity. It imposes no divergence condition on $L$: the projected equation removes its gradient part when solving for the divergence-free velocity. Values of the underlying function outside $[0,1]$ are unrestricted.
e03-appa-forcing-continuity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: The source $L$ is a curve on $[0,1]$ in vector-valued $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$, continuous in that spatial norm. The formal statement requires exactly this time continuity. It imposes no divergence condition on $L$: the projected equation removes its gradient part when solving for the divergence-free velocity. Values of the underlying function outside $[0,1]$ are unrestricted.

e03-appa-a1-existence-uniqueness.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: The paper assumes symmetric $K$, skew-symmetric $\Omega$ and coefficient continuity in $C^{1,1/2}$. The formal result constructs the same zero endpoint displacement, solenoidal constant and unique periodic pressure gradient from positive ellipticity, the energy inequality for all $H^1_0$ paths, continuity in $C^{0,1/2}$ and bounded first spatial derivatives. It does not separately require the symmetry conditions. It also supplies a zero-mean potential, but uniqueness is asserted for the gradient rather than arbitrary scalar normalizations.
e03-appa-a1-existence-uniqueness.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: Under the same symmetry, ellipticity and $H^1_0$ energy conditions, the formal statement gives the existence and uniqueness classes printed here. It requires only coefficient continuity in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatial differentiability and uniform coefficient and first derivative bounds. The paper's continuity in $C^{1,1/2}$ is stronger. Uniqueness is equality of $z,v,c$ and $\nabla\phi$ on $[0,1]$, not equality of unnormalized scalar potentials outside that interval.
e03-appa-a1-existence-uniqueness.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1: Under the same symmetry, ellipticity and $H^1_0$ energy conditions, the formal statement gives the existence and uniqueness classes printed here. It requires only coefficient continuity in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatial differentiability and uniform coefficient and first derivative bounds. The paper's continuity in $C^{1,1/2}$ is stronger. Uniqueness is equality of $z,v,c$ and $\nabla\phi$ on $[0,1]$, not equality of unnormalized scalar potentials outside that interval.

e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: Every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives a unique velocity, zero endpoint displacement, constant solenoidal field and pressure gradient satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$, where $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv$. Its projected solution has zero terminal primitive, and the recovered periodic gradient yields the full displayed equation and both endpoint conditions.
e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces.TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution: On $[0,T]$, a solution here consists of a continuous curve $v$ of weakly divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$ fields and a fixed divergence-free field $c$, satisfying $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$ and $Jv(T)=0$. The paper states the full pressure equation and endpoint conditions. This formal formulation records a continuous divergence-free velocity, its zero terminal primitive and the projected equation; recovering the pressure gradient and proving existence are separate steps.
e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces.TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedMomentum: The paper displays an equation together with divergence and endpoint constraints. This formal expression is only its left side, $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L$; the equation and constraints belong to the solution statement.
e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: Each $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,G$ on this interval satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z(0)=z(1)=0$, with solenoidal $z,c$ and periodic $G=\nabla\phi$. The equation and the two zero displacement traces agree with the selected display. The exported uniqueness concerns the solution interval.
e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces.TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution: The condition requires continuous $v,G$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, and $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. Taking $T=1$ gives exactly the displayed system. This declaration specifies satisfaction of that system. The theorem separately asserts a solution exists.

e03-appa-a1-polynomial-estimate.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: For positive ellipticity and displacement coercivity, the formal estimate is $\|z_t\|_0\le CQ^{291}\|L\|_0$, with $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$. These four coefficient bounds control values and first spatial derivatives. The paper uses full $C_tC^{1,1/2}$ norms and an unspecified exponent. The formal result needs only time continuity in $C^{0,1/2}$ and does not separately require symmetric $K$ or skew-symmetric $\Omega$. Thus it retains the conclusion under weaker hypotheses and sharper coefficient controls.
e03-appa-a1-polynomial-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: The formal statement retains symmetry of $K$, skew-symmetry of $\Omega$, positive ellipticity and the energy inequality for all zero endpoint Sobolev paths. Its bound has the printed form with an absolute nonnegative integer exponent, but $Q$ uses separate uniform value and first spatial derivative bounds. Coefficient continuity is required only in $C^{0,1/2}$. Consequently the paper's stronger continuity and full $C^{1,1/2}$ controls give a special case of this formal estimate.

e03-appa-a1-smooth-conclusion.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: For smooth periodic coefficients and source, positive ellipticity and the energy inequality on every $H^1_0$ path suffice for the formal result to give smooth $z,c$ and $\nabla\phi$ on the closed unit slab. It does not separately require symmetric $K$ or skew-symmetric $\Omega$, unlike the paper's standing hypotheses. Smoothness and uniqueness concern the gradient; a potential is chosen with zero spatial mean, while an arbitrary time-dependent additive normalization is not fixed.
e03-appa-a1-smooth-conclusion.TorusEuler.exists_paperA1_smoothSolution: The paper concludes smoothness of $z,c$ and $\nabla\phi$. This formal existence result gives an integrated projected solution with a jointly smooth velocity under smooth coefficients and source, positive ellipticity and the $H^1_0$ energy bound. It omits separate symmetry hypotheses, but does not state all three smoothness conclusions here. Those are supplied by the full endpoint theorem after recovering displacement, constant field and pressure.
e03-appa-a1-smooth-conclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1: Under the added joint smoothness of $K,\Omega,L$ on the closed slab, the statement concludes joint smoothness of $z,G=\nabla\phi$ and spatial smoothness of the time-independent $c$, exactly as in this sentence.

e03-appa-displacement-recovery.TorusEuler.paperA1_displacement_eq_primi: If $v$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, $z_t=v$ there with derivatives taken within the interval, and $z(0)=0$, then $z(t)=\int_0^tv(s)\,ds$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. It supplies the asserted identity $z=Jv$ from the initial condition and $z_t=v$, without using the terminal condition.

e03-appa-subtract-time-mean.TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean: The formal formula on a positive interval is $\mathcal Qv=v-T^{-1}\int_0^Tv$. At $T=1$ it is exactly the time-average subtraction in Appendix A. The general definition also has a value at $T=0$ because its reciprocal is assigned zero there; none of the positive-interval endpoint conclusions rely on that degenerate case.

e03-appa-remove-pressure-gradient.TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_C1_gradi: Periodicity is needed: a constant vector field is a gradient of a nonperiodic affine function, but the torus Leray projection preserves that constant field. This is the precise meaning of removal of the periodic pressure gradient in the selected phrase.

e03-appa-projections-commute.TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialProjectio: The paper uses commutation on $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$. The formal result proves that orthogonal spatial Leray projection and time-average subtraction commute on space-time $L^2$ for every positive interval length $T$. The normalization $T^{-1}$ in the average is included, so the paper's two projections are recovered when $T=1$.

e03-appa-compressed-equation.TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient: At each spatial label, let $K$ and $\Omega$ be bounded operators on $L^2([0,T];\mathbb R^3)$, varying half-Hölder continuously with the label, and take $T\ge0$. Define $B=K-J\Omega$, where $J$ integrates a time path from zero. Thus $J$ acts after $\Omega$. When these operators are multiplication by the time-dependent matrices, this is $Bv=Kv-J(\Omega v)$ in Appendix A. The formula does not impose zero time mean, divergence freedom or coercivity; those are separate ingredients in the projected equation $\mathcal RBv=-\mathcal RL$. The paper states the projected equation, the projection constraint and the formula for $B$. This formal expression supplies only $B=K-J\Omega$ on time paths. The other assertions come from the projected solution construction.

e03-appa-primitive-adjoint.TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_eq_: Let $T\ge0$ and let $u,v\in L^2([0,T];E)$ for a complete real Hilbert space. The paper gives a pointwise adjoint formula. The formal result proves the corresponding pairing identity $\langle Ju,v\rangle=-\langle u,Jv\rangle$ for zero-mean $v$, which is enough for the energy calculation but does not itself state the pointwise formula.

e03-appa-energy-identity.TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_: For a zero-time-mean velocity $w$, its primitive $Jw$ has both traces zero. The projected mixed operator paired with $w$ therefore gives the kinetic and vorticity terms in the displayed time integral. The identity turns the separate displacement-energy lower bound into an operator coercivity estimate.
e03-appa-energy-identity.TorusEuler.EndpointSobolevEnergyBound: For every label $a\in\mathbb T^3$ and every $v\in L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ with $\int_0^1v=0$, require $\int_0^1(Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot Jv)\,dt\ge\mu\|v\|_{L^2}^2$, where $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv$. This specifies the lower-bound assumption. It does not itself prove the equality between the operator pairing and the energy integral.

r5-B-two-projected-inversions.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2: The formal statement treats $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$ on $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$ on $L^2(0,1;\mathbb R^3)$-valued fields, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time mean. For a Lipschitz coefficient coercive on all of $\mathbb R^3$ in the spatial case and on zero-time-mean paths in the mixed case, it proves that $v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ is invertible on the projected half-Hölder space, with a polynomial bound. The sentence identifies the common equation. The declaration additionally proves its inversion.

r5-B-frozen-fourier-coefficients.TorusEuler.complexifiedHalfHolderFourier: For a spatially constant bounded linear operator $B$ on a real Hilbert space $H$ and $v\in C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;H)$, the formal statement gives $\widehat{Bv}(n)=B_{\mathbb C}\widehat v(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. This includes $H=L^2(0,1;\mathbb R^3)$, so an operator acting on whole time paths still preserves each spatial mode. The sentence concerns the full projected equation $\mathcal R(Bv)=f$; this declaration proves the coefficient identity, and the Fourier symbol of $\mathcal R$ is a separate part of its diagonalization.

e03-r2-appa-two-hilbert-spaces.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: The formal statement treats exactly two coefficient spaces on $\mathbb T^3$: bounded operators on $\mathbb R^3$ with projection $\mathbb P$, and bounded operators on $L^2((0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ with projection $\mathbb P\mathcal Q$. Here $\mathbb P$ is spatial Leray projection and $\mathcal Qw=w-\int_0^1w(t)\,dt$. The path space identifies functions agreeing almost everywhere, so the inclusion of the time endpoint does not change $L^2$. The projected fields in the second setting are spatially divergence free and have zero time mean.
e03-r2-appa-two-hilbert-spaces.TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean: The paper introduces two Hilbert-space settings and their projections. This formal expression defines only subtraction of the time mean. The two settings and the combined spatial projection appear in the full statement of Lemma A.2.

e03-r2-appa-coefficient-hypothesis.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: The paper's coefficient assumption is $B\in C^{1,1/2}$ with $\mu>0$. For the base inverse the formal statement only asks that the half-Hölder coefficient be spatially Lipschitz, together with the same positive coercivity in the following hypothesis. It therefore does not assert the displayed stronger regularity assumption. The inverse theorem has broader scope, while its higher-order clause still asks for $C^{k,1/2}$ regularity.

e03-appa-a2-coercivity.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder: The paper imposes coercivity in either of two Hilbert-space settings. This formal theorem treats only $H=\mathbb R^3$ with the spatial Leray projection. The time-path case is a separate theorem.
e03-appa-a2-coercivity.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder: The paper allows spatial vectors or time paths. This formal theorem treats only $H=L^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$, with coercivity tested on zero-time-mean paths as required there. The spatial-vector case is separate.
e03-appa-a2-coercivity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: For $H=\mathbb R^3$, the formal hypothesis is $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ for every label $a$ and every vector $w$. For $H=L^2(0,1;\mathbb R^3)$, the same inequality is required for every label and every path with $\int_0^1w=0$. In both cases $\mu>0$, and no symmetry of $B$ is required. These are exactly (A.4) with the test class stated immediately after that display in the paper.

e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder: Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$ and $B(a)w\cdot w\ge\mu|w|^2$ for every label and vector, with $\mu>0$. The paper gives the inverse in both Hilbert-space settings. This formal result provides it only for spatial vector fields with the Leray projection. The inverse on whole time paths is supplied separately.
e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder: Let $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, with $\mathcal Q$ subtracting the time average. Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(H))$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ for zero-mean paths, with $\mu>0$. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on $\mathcal RC^{0,1/2}$ and $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+\|D_aB\|_\infty)^{145}\|\mathcal RBv\|$. This is only the time-path case of Lemma A.2. The constant is independent of the coefficient and datum; higher regularity and the spatial-vector case are separate results. The paper gives the inverse for both spatial vectors and time paths. This formal result covers the divergence-free, zero-time-mean path case only. The spatial-vector inverse is supplied separately.
e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$. The paper states the base inverse for $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficients. The formal result requires only spatial Lipschitz regularity and bounds the inverse using the coefficient supremum and Lipschitz constant, so the paper's setting is included.
e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2: The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$. The paper states the base inverse for $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficients. The formal result requires only spatial Lipschitz regularity and bounds the inverse using the coefficient supremum and Lipschitz constant, so the paper's setting is included.
e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism.TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion: The first requirement is precisely the base isomorphism in the selected sentence. This is a definition of the conclusion, which Lemma A.2 then proves under its hypotheses.

e03-appa-a2-base-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder: Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$ and $B(a)w\cdot w\ge\mu|w|^2$ for every label and vector, with $\mu>0$. Then $v\mapsto\mathbb P(Bv)$ is invertible on divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}$ fields, with $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+\|D_aB\|_\infty)^{145}\|\mathbb P(Bv)\|$. The constant is chosen before $B,\mu$ and the datum. This proves the spatial-vector case of Lemma A.2 and fixes a polynomial exponent where the paper leaves it unspecified. The time-path case and higher norms are separate statements. The paper gives (A.5) for both allowed Hilbert spaces. e03-appa-a2-base-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder: Let $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, with $\mathcal Q$ subtracting the time average. Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(H))$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ for zero-mean paths, with $\mu>0$. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on $\mathcal RC^{0,1/2}$ and $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+\|D_aB\|_\infty)^{145}\|\mathcal RBv\|$. This is only the time-path case of Lemma A.2. The constant is independent of the coefficient and datum; higher regularity and the spatial-vector case are separate results. The paper gives (A.5) in two settings. e03-appa-a2-base-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2: The paper's estimate assumes $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficients and uses their $C^1$ norm. The formal base theorem allows Lipschitz coefficients and uses their supremum and Lipschitz bounds, which the paper's $C^1$ control supplies.

e03-appa-a2-higher-isomorphism.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b: The paper asserts a higher Hölder isomorphism for both Hilbert spaces. This formal result gives the inverse bound for spatial vectors; boundedness of the forward map and the time-path case are supplied separately.

e03-appa-a2-higher-isomorphism.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.freezingConclu: The paper concludes the higher Hölder isomorphism. c8-holder-coercive-testing.TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWeakErrorEstim: The paper displays the energy pairing with coefficient $\mu$. e03-appa-leray-symbol.TorusEuler.angularLeray: Thus it projects vectors orthogonally onto $\xi^\perp$. At a nonzero lattice frequency $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, this is the orthogonal projection onto $n^\perp$ used in the paper.

e03-appa-frozen-symbol.TorusEuler.frozenSymbol: For bounded operators $r,B$ on a real Hilbert space, define $A=rBr+I-r$. On the range of a projection, $A$ acts as the projected coefficient; on its kernel, $A$ is the identity. The formula itself allows arbitrary $r,B$. e03-appa-identity-on-complement.TorusEuler.frozenSymbol_apply_of_proj_eq: For the orthogonal Fourier projection in Lemma A.2, its kernel is the orthogonal complement of its range, so the statement proves the paper's assertion that the extended frozen coefficient acts as the identity on that complement.
