e03-appa-full-symbol-coercivity.TorusEuler.frozenSymbol_coercive: The paper displays the complex real-part estimate and an intermediate two-term lower bound. This formal result gives the final lower bound in a real Hilbert space. The passage to complex Fourier coefficients is handled separately.

e03-appa-frozen-inverse-bound.TorusEuler.norm_complexFrozenInverseSymb: The positivity of $\mu$ makes the reciprocal an ordinary positive inverse. Symmetry of $B$ is not a hypothesis of this coercive inverse bound.

e03-appa-smooth-projection.TorusEuler.contDiffOn_angularLeray: The paper uses projection symbols in both the spatial-vector and time-path cases. The formal result proves smoothness only for $I-\widehat\xi\otimes\widehat\xi$, the spatial Leray symbol, but on all $\xi\ne0$, not merely the unit sphere. e03-appa-inverse-derivative.TorusEuler.fderiv_frozenSymbol_inverse_a: The paper differentiates the inverse with respect to frequency. e03-appa-five-angular-derivatives.TorusEuler.complexFrozenSymbols_fiveJets: With a smooth orthogonal projection whose derivatives through order five have bounds $D^i$, $D\ge1$, and a coefficient coercive by $\mu>0$ on its range, the formal result bounds both complex inverse symbols through order five by constants times $(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|)^{11}$. The constants are explicit functions of $D$. For the fixed projection used in the paper, its angular derivative bounds are dimensional constants; they must be supplied before this estimate is applied.

e03-appa-frozen-multiplier-bound.TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo: With the paper's homogeneous projection and $B_0=B(a_0)$, the operator identification and $\|B_0\|\le\|B\|_\infty$ give (A.6). e03-appa-dyadic-kernel-decay.TorusEuler.scaledMultiplierKernel_decay: The paper has already incorporated the symbol derivative bounds into $CC_0$. e03-appa-dyadic-half-power.TorusEuler.norm_operatorLiftConvolution_: At scale $\Lambda>0$, convolution with the rescaled kernel is bounded by $H\Lambda^{-1/2}\int\|G(y)\|\,|y|^{1/2}\,dy$. e03-appa-zero-mode-bound.TorusEuler.norm_complexFrozenInverseSymb: Take the frequency to be zero. In the spatial-vector case $r(0)=I$; in the time-path case it is the projection subtracting the time mean. Thus this estimates exactly the zero-mode action described by the paper.

e03-appa-localization-cutoff.TorusEuler.freezingCutoff: The paper proceeds to require a gradient bound on the cutoff. The formal construction chooses the clipped distance function $\chi(a)=\max(0,\min(1,2-d(a,a_0)/r))$. For $r>0$ it has the stated values and support but is only Lipschitz at the transition radii. The accompanying formal estimates use differences rather than a classical gradient everywhere.

e03-r2-appa-cutoff-one.TorusEuler.freezingCutoff_eq_one: Let $r>0$, and use $\chi(a)=\max\{0,\min\{1,2-d(a,a_0)/r\}\}$. If $d(a,a_0)\le r$, then $\chi(a)=1$. The statement concerns only the values of this cutoff; no smoothness of the cutoff or coefficient and no inverse estimate is required.

e03-r2-appa-cutoff-support.TorusEuler.freezingCutoff_eq_zero: In particular the nonzero set lies inside the open $2r$-ball. The closed support is contained in the closed $2r$-ball. The sentence does not require an additional margin inside that ball.

e03-r2-appa-cutoff-range.TorusEuler.freezingCutoff_mem_Icc: On a metric space, for every center $a_0$, every real radius $r$ and every point $a$, the expression $\chi(a)=\max\{0,\min\{1,2-d(a,a_0)/r\}\}$ lies in $[0,1]$. Positive radius is needed for the inner-ball, outer-ball and Lipschitz conclusions used in (A.7). The statement here bounds the two factors $\chi$ and $1-\chi$; it does not by itself provide spatial localization.

e03-appa-cutoff-gradient-variant.TorusEuler.freezingCutoff_lipschitz: The paper writes a pointwise gradient bound for the cutoff. The formal proof uses a clipped radial cutoff and proves $|\chi(x)-\chi(y)|\le r^{-1}d(x,y)$ instead, so the localization relies on Lipschitz control rather than differentiability of that cutoff.

e03-appa-localized-identity.TorusEuler.freezingHalfHolderMultipliers: The paper writes the frozen identity after splitting the error into near and far parts. The formal identity keeps a single coefficient-error source. The displayed version follows by the separate source decomposition and linearity.
e03-appa-localized-identity.TorusEuler.exists_freezing_split_sources: The paper displays the complete inverse identity for $v$. This formal result constructs and estimates only the near and far error sources, which must be substituted into the separately proved frozen identity.

e03-appa-localized-coefficient-bounds.TorusEuler.localizedCoefficient_holderHa: Assume $B$ is Lipschitz with constant $L$ and a cutoff takes values in $[0,1]$, vanishes beyond distance $2r$, and has Lipschitz bound $C/r$, with $r>0$. e03-appa-far-source-vanishes.TorusEuler.exists_freezing_split_sources: For a Lipschitz coefficient $B$, half-Hölder field $v$ and $0<r\le1$, the formal decomposition constructs a far source that vanishes throughout the closed ball of radius $r$. Its sum with the near source is $(B(a_0)-B)v$. Applying the frozen inverse to these two sources gives the last two terms in (A.7); their construction alone does not include that inverse identity.

e03-appa-far-source-radius.TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo: The paper controls pairs with separation at most $r/2$ and states the resulting half-Hölder contribution. The formal off-support estimate assumes the source vanishes on an $r$-ball and gives a Lipschitz increment bound only when the separation is at most $r/4$. Combining that bound with the far-source supremum estimate gives the same $r^{-1/2}$ order on this smaller range. Treating the remaining pairs requires adjusting the radius split and constants. e03-appa-remaining-supremum.TorusEuler.halfHolder_norm_le_of_frozen_: The paper includes polynomial control of the remaining constant in terms of $Q_0$. e03-appa-holder-l2-interpolation.TorusEuler.unitTorus_sup_le_holderHalf_a: The formal inequality requires $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and a supplied half-Hölder seminorm bound $H$, and gives $\|v\|_\infty\le\varepsilon H+\varepsilon^{-3}\|v\|_{L^2}$ on the unit torus with normalized measure. e03-appa-mixed-norm-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder: The paper expresses (A.8) in terms of $K$, $\Omega$ and the time supremum of $L$. The formal time-path inverse estimate uses the coefficient $B$ and projected datum directly, so the coefficient and source comparisons are needed to obtain the displayed bound.
e03-appa-mixed-norm-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The paper writes the complete velocity estimate (A.8). At this stage the formal proof bounds the mixed inverse using its coefficient supremum and Lipschitz constant. The source estimate and conversion to the displayed parameter $Q$ are completed in later steps.

e03-appa-recover-constant.TorusEuler.endpointProjectedWeak_eq_mean: If $w\in L^2([0,T];E)$ satisfies $w-T^{-1}\int_0^Tw=0$ in that space, then $w(t)=T^{-1}\int_0^Tw$ for almost every time. The paper gives the formula for the spatially projected constant field. The formal result recovers the average of an already projected $L^2$ time path almost everywhere; commuting the projection with integration and proving spatial Hölder regularity of $c$ are separate steps.

e03-appa-instantaneous-equation.TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstant_of_subtra: The formal statement gives this equation almost everywhere in time, as in the surrounding paper text, after a square-integrable projected momentum path has zero time-average subtraction. For a general positive interval it defines $c$ as the time average $T^{-1}\int_0^Tw$. At $T=1$ this is the paper's constant. Continuity is not concluded until the following inverse-recovery argument.

e03-appa-time-holder-increment.TorusEuler.continuous_and_norm_sub_le_en: Let $w$ be a spatially half-Hölder field with values in $L^2([0,T];E)$. Its primitive $Jw(t)$ is continuous in the spatial $C^{0,1/2}$ norm and satisfies $\|Jw(t)-Jw(s)\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le|t-s|^{1/2}\|w\|_{C^{0,1/2}(L^2)}$ for $s,t\in[0,T]$. The half-Hölder norm is the maximum of supremum and seminorm. The formal statement allows an arbitrary metric label space, including the unit torus. Applied to $w=\Omega v$, this makes the right side of (A.9) continuous before continuity of $v$ has been recovered. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. Take $w=\Omega v$ and $T=1$. This yields the displayed time increment bound in the same spatial half-Hölder norm.

e03-r2-appa-fixed-time-inverse.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The proof constructs the family $S(t)v=\mathbb P(K(t)v)$ on solenoidal half-Hölder fields from the spatial inverse of Lemma A.2. The quoted definition occurs inside that construction. The declaration's exported assertion is the full endpoint theorem.
e03-r2-appa-fixed-time-inverse.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_solenoi: The paper introduces a family of fixed-time operators. This formal result transfers one supplied freezing inverse to divergence-free fields; constructing the family and establishing uniform time-dependent bounds are additional steps in Theorem A.1.

e03-appa-inverse-time-continuity.TorusEuler.continuousOn_endpointFixedInv: The formal result says that a family of bounded Banach-space isomorphisms continuous in operator norm has inverses continuous in operator norm. Applying it here requires the already established isomorphism $S(t)v=\mathbb P(K(t)v)$ on solenoidal half-Hölder fields and the continuity of that forward family. Coefficient continuity alone would not establish invertibility.

e03-appa-continuous-representative.TorusEuler.exists_endpointContinuousRepr: The paper asserts continuity and the final estimate (A.3). The formal recovery result constructs the continuous representative with a bound in terms of the inverse, constant field and source contributions. The preceding estimates are needed to combine these into $CQ^p\|L\|_0$.

e03-appa-weak-elliptic-injectivity.TorusEuler.endpointProjectedHilbertOpera: The paper applies the displayed energy calculation to the difference of the two velocities. The formal result states abstract injectivity of the projected coercive Hilbert-space operator; identifying that particular difference and equation is a separate application.

e03-appa-recovered-endpoint-traces.TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_ha: The formal statement assumes a continuous velocity in the strong spatial space, agreement almost everywhere through an injective bounded embedding with the weak zero-mean velocity, and zero integral of the latter. It then proves $Jv(0)=Jv(T)=0$ and $(Jv)_t=v$ on the closed interval. This is exactly the endpoint recovery after the preceding continuous-representative construction.

e03-appa-recover-pressure.TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e: For time-continuous half-Hölder coefficients and source, an existing projected endpoint solution gives a periodic scalar potential whose gradient is continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$ and completes $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$. The formal result also chooses the potential with zero spatial mean at every time, a normalization not imposed in this sentence. It does not separately assert time differentiability of the potential.
e03-appa-recover-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The exported solution includes a continuous periodic pressure gradient completing the displayed momentum equation. Its proof obtains that gradient from the vanishing Leray projection. The scalar potential remains free up to time-dependent constants.

e03-appa-uniqueness-through-recovery.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: Its uniqueness clause compares any other projected solution and any gradient completing its equation. Equality of the velocity, primitive displacement, constant and gradient holds on $[0,1]$; arbitrary scalar potentials are not compared.
e03-appa-uniqueness-through-recovery.TorusEuler.paperA1_solution_of_unproject: The paper concludes uniqueness of all recovered quantities. This formal result converts any displacement-and-pressure solution into a projected solution with the same velocity and constant. The inverse theorem supplies the uniqueness needed to finish the argument.
e03-appa-uniqueness-through-recovery.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The proof converts any competing unprojected solution into the projected solution class. Uniqueness there gives equality of velocity, displacement, constant and gradient on $[0,1]$, which is the claim of the selected sentence.

e03-appa-smooth-inverse.TorusEuler.contDiffOn_endpointFixedInver: The paper asserts smooth inversion for the particular operators $S(t)$ on every higher spatial Hölder space. The formal result is a Banach-space inversion theorem. If a family of bounded isomorphisms is $C^n$ in operator norm, then its inverses are $C^n$. Establishing the family and its forward regularity on each $C^{k,1/2}$ space is an additional premise in this application.
e03-appa-smooth-inverse.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The paper invokes smooth inversion on every higher spatial Hölder space. The formal proof instead recovers successive spatial derivatives using the base $C^{0,1/2}$ inverse and combines their regularity, so it reaches smoothness by a different intermediate route.

e03-appa-primitive-derivative-gain.TorusEuler.contDiffOn_endpointPrimitive_: For a Banach-space-valued $C^n$ function $f$ on a positive closed interval, the formal statement proves $Jf\in C^{n+1}$, with endpoint derivatives taken from within the interval. Applying it to $f=\Omega v$ requires that product to have the preceding time regularity in the chosen spatial norm. It supplies exactly the one-derivative gain used in the paper.

e03-appa-all-time-derivatives.TorusEuler.contDiffOn_endpointVelocity_a: The paper concludes regularity in every spatial Hölder norm and smoothness of the pressure gradient. This formal time-regularity result gives smooth $v$ and $Jv$ in a supplied Banach space. The spatial estimates and pressure recovery are additional steps.
e03-appa-all-time-derivatives.TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1: For jointly smooth coefficients and source, it explicitly concludes smoothness of displacement, the constant field and the periodic gradient. The selected sentence describes the time-regularity step leading to that exported conclusion.
e03-appa-all-time-derivatives.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of: The exported smooth-data clause gives the smooth displacement, constant field and gradient. Spatial and time differentiations are combined in the proof. This is a proof of the final conclusion, not a separate statement of each higher-order time estimate.

e03-r2-appb-cutoff-symbol.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixB.CutoffSymbol: The paper fixes a radial cutoff symbol with the stated smoothness, range and support. The formal condition retains those properties but asks only for evenness, so it also admits nonradial symbols.
The paper imposes radiality as well as the range, plateau and support conditions. The formal statement proves that those hypotheses imply the weaker even-symbol conditions. It does not say that every admitted symbol is radial or construct a particular cutoff.

e03-appb-multiplier-definition.TorusEuler.smoothFourierCutoff: For $\Lambda\ge1$ and the paper's supported symbol, the formal finite sum has exactly the stated multiplier on every integer frequency. Its definition for arbitrary symbols or zero scale is broader, but those values are outside the paper's assumptions.
e03-appb-multiplier-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The paper defines the multiplier for $\Lambda\ge1$. The formal statement proves the Fourier coefficient identity for every $\Lambda>0$ and every admitted even symbol, including the paper's radial symbols; for real velocities the coefficient identity is stated after embedding the values in a complex vector space.

e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_commutes_: The paper states derivative commutation. For a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field with a $C^m$ periodic lift, this result identifies its $m$th cutoff derivative with convolution of its $m$th derivative. Interpreting that convolution as the derivative field's cutoff is a further identification; no time derivative is asserted.
e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_derivativ: The paper states derivative commutation. This result gives the spatial derivative-tensor convolution identity for a complex Banach-valued field under a $C^{m,1/2}$ hypothesis. It neither states time commutation nor uses the minimal $C^m$ spatial hypothesis.
e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.hasDerivWithinAt_realVectorFo: The paper states commutation with derivatives. This result proves one time derivative commutes for smooth real velocities on a nondegenerate closed interval, including one-sided derivatives at its endpoints.
e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_realVectorFourier: The paper states commutation with derivatives. This result proves the identity for one coordinate derivative of a continuously differentiable periodic real velocity, using its continuous derivative on the torus.
e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The paper states derivative commutation without separating the cases. The formal statement gives all spatial orders for complex Banach-valued fields and first spatial and time derivatives for real velocities; further real orders follow by repeated application to smooth fields.
e03-appb-commutation.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1: The paper states commutation with derivatives for its radial cutoff and $\Lambda\ge1$. The formal theorem permits even symbols and every $\Lambda>0$, while treating arbitrary complex spatial orders and first real spatial and time derivatives separately; higher real orders require iteration.

e03-appb-parity-support.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_admis: The paper lists parity, divergence freeness and frequency support. This result supplies oddness, divergence freeness and support for smooth real velocities; preservation of evenness is provided by the separate parity result.
e03-appb-parity-support.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_support_p: The paper lists parity, divergence freeness and frequency support. This result supplies parity and the support bound for complex Banach-valued fields, while the real-velocity divergence statement is proved separately.
e03-appb-parity-support.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_parit: The paper lists parity, divergence freeness and frequency support. This result proves parity for real velocities. The frequency bound and preservation of divergence freeness are separate conclusions.
e03-appb-parity-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The paper requires a radial symbol and $\Lambda\ge1$ for these properties. The formal statement proves them for even symbols and every $\Lambda>0$, with divergence preservation for smooth real velocities, so the paper’s setting is included.

e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_LInfinity: For $\Lambda>0$ and smooth $\psi$ supported in the radius-two ball, this result gives only $\|S_\Lambda g\|_{L^\infty}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$ on the unit-volume torus. The input is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded, with a complex normed target. The formal estimate omits completeness. The ordinary Fourier-integral interpretation uses a Banach target, since the integral convention assigns zero in an incomplete target. The paper's Hölder bound is a separate conclusion.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_LInfi: The paper gives both the $L^\infty$ and half-Hölder operator bounds. This result proves the essential-supremum bound for real velocities, while the Hölder bound is supplied separately.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff: Let $\Lambda>0$, let $\psi$ be smooth and supported in the radius-two ball, and let $g$ be almost-everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded on the unit-volume torus, with a real normed target. This result bounds the operator obtained by integrating the real part of the finite spectral kernel: its $L^\infty$ bound is $\|\check\psi\|_{L^1}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$. For an even symbol and a Banach target this is the paper's cutoff. Without evenness the symbol is symmetrized; in an incomplete target the formal integral convention assigns zero. No Hölder bound is included.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder: The paper gives both operator bounds. This result proves preservation of $C^{0,1/2}$ and its norm bound for complex Banach-valued fields. The measurable-input $L^\infty$ estimate is separate.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: For a smooth even symbol $\psi$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside radius two, the formal statement gives both operator bounds on the unit torus for every $\Lambda>0$, with one constant depending only on $\psi$. Its $L^\infty$ clause requires almost-everywhere strong measurability and a complex Banach target. The real-velocity branch assumes continuity and gives the uniform and half-Hölder bounds. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$ without this split between target classes. The separately linked real-input result supplies its measurable-velocity clause.

e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m: For a continuous field in a real normed space with frequencies at most $4\Lambda$, $\Lambda\ge1$, the formal estimate is (B.1), with each multi-index counted once. The frequency condition is imposed on every continuous linear scalar measurement. The constant is chosen before the target space, frequency and field.
e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein: The paper counts each multi-index once and allows every normed target. This result bounds the larger sum over all ordered coordinate differentiations, but restricts the target to a complex Banach space. It implies (B.1) for that class after discarding repeated terms. The separate real normed-space theorem has the paper's broader target scope.
e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The paper states (B.1) for a radial symbol and $\Lambda\ge1$. The formal statement retains arbitrary real normed target spaces and the multi-index sum, and extends the assumptions to even symbols and every $\Lambda>0$.

e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail: The paper states the $C^{M,1/2}$ cutoff tail estimate. This result gives it for continuous complex Banach-valued torus fields with $\Lambda\ge1$, including finiteness of the output norm. It does not itself state the real-velocity estimate used in the construction.
e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_realVec: For the real three-dimensional velocities used in the paper, the formal statement gives (B.2) and the asserted output Hölder regularity for every $\Lambda>0$, extending the paper's $\Lambda\ge1$ range. It requires a smooth supported symbol with a unit plateau, but not radiality.
e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The paper gives (B.2) in a radial-symbol setting at $\Lambda\ge1$. The formal statement spells out complex Banach-valued and real three-dimensional velocity versions and permits even symbols and all $\Lambda>0$. It does not state a tail estimate for every real normed target, unlike the explicit target generality of its Bernstein clause.

e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m: The paper specifies uniform constants for both Bernstein and tail estimates. This result chooses the Bernstein constant before the target space, frequency and input. The tail constant is supplied by a separate theorem.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail: The paper specifies uniform constants for both estimates. This result gives the tail constant uniformly in $s\le M$, frequency and input, while the Bernstein constant is chosen separately.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: The formal statement selects the operator, Bernstein and tail constants after the symbol and before the frequency, target spaces and fields. The tail constant is selected by $M$ and is uniform over every $s\le M$, matching the dependence asserted in the paper.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The proof chooses the constants from integrals of the fixed kernel and its derivatives before introducing the frequency or field. It therefore establishes the paper's asserted uniformity in those inputs, with a tail constant depending on $M$ rather than on the lower order $s$.

e03-r2-appb-proof-symmetries.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The paper derives parity, divergence preservation and derivative commutation from the scalar, even symbol. The formal proof establishes these properties in complex and real formulations, giving arbitrary spatial orders for complex fields and first spatial and time derivatives for real velocities; higher real orders follow by iteration.

e03-r2-appb-proof-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The paper obtains the support bound from the symbol support. The formal statement proves zero output coefficients for $|\xi|>2\Lambda$, for every $\Lambda>0$, in both its complex Banach and real-velocity branches. This includes the paper's $\Lambda\ge1$ range. The proof uses the finite frequency sum and the vanishing symbol outside the cutoff ball.

e03-r2-appb-kernel-definition.TorusEuler.cutoffSchwartzKernel: The formal object is the inverse Fourier transform of the smooth real symbol, interpreted as a complex-valued Schwartz function. Smoothness and vanishing outside the radius-two ball are its hypotheses; these are included in the paper's symbol assumptions.

e03-r2-appb-kernel-dilation.TorusEuler.scaledLiftKernel: The formal formula is exactly $K_\Lambda(y)=\Lambda^3K(\Lambda y)$. The expression also exists at nonpositive scales, but all analytic uses in Appendix B have positive $\Lambda$; the zero-scale expression is identically zero.

e03-r2-appb-convolution-representation.TorusEuler.liftConvolution_cutoffSchwart: The paper represents the cutoff by convolution of the periodic field. This result proves that identity for continuous complex Banach-valued fields. The real-velocity version is obtained through the corresponding real-valued cutoff.

e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup: The paper applies convolution to both values and spatial increments to obtain two operator bounds. This result supplies the uniform bound for continuous fields. The increment and Hölder estimates are separate.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup: The paper obtains both the uniform and Hölder bounds from convolution. This result supplies only the uniform estimate for real velocities, with the same frequency-independent kernel constant.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound: The paper obtains both operator bounds by estimating convolution on values and spatial increments. The formal statement proves a pointwise output bound from an integrable complex input bounded almost everywhere, with constant $\|\check\psi\|_{L^1}$. It has no spatial-increment conclusion and does not itself give the Hölder estimate.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: For smooth even $\psi$, $0\le\psi\le1$, with unit plateau and radius-two support, the formal proof obtains uniform and half-Hölder cutoff bounds on the unit torus for every $\Lambda>0$. Its essential-supremum clause treats almost-everywhere strongly measurable, essentially bounded complex Banach-valued fields; its real-velocity branch assumes continuity. The quoted proof does not separate these classes. A supplied separate theorem gives the real measurable-input estimate. Kernel-mass scaling is another declaration, so this proof is not itself the isolated equality $\|K_\Lambda\|_1=\|K\|_1$.

e03-appb-kernel-derivative-scale.TorusEuler.integral_norm_iteratedFDeriv_: The paper writes the scaling identity for a coordinate derivative of the cutoff kernel at scale $4\Lambda$. The formal statement proves the same identity for any complex Schwartz kernel, any fixed list of derivative directions, and every positive scale. Taking coordinate directions and the scale $4\Lambda$ gives the displayed equality.
e03-appb-kernel-derivative-scale.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The paper displays the exact scaling identity for kernel derivatives. The formal proof uses a Bernstein estimate derived from that identity and sums the coordinate bounds. The separate kernel theorem states the scaling identity itself.

e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal: At a fixed point, subtract the Taylor polynomial of $f(x-y)$ from the convolution integrand. Kernel mass one recovers $f(x)$, and the vanishing moments cancel the terms of positive degree below $k$. This lemma bounds what remains using the $k$th derivative and the absolute $k$th moment. The Hölder bound also needs the corresponding estimate for increments.

This is the estimate for the difference of two Taylor remainders, evaluated at $x$ and $x+h$. The bound uses a Hölder estimate on the highest derivative and gains the increment factor. Applying the value and increment lemmas at each derivative order through $s$ yields the two parts of the $C^{s,1/2}$ bound.
e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz: The integral of $K_\Lambda(y)=\Lambda^3\check\psi(\Lambda y)$ over $\mathbb R^3$ equals $\psi(0)$ for every positive scale. The cutoff used here has $\psi(0)=1$, so the constant term of the Taylor expansion integrates to $f(x)$. The identity requires smoothness and support of the symbol, with no radiality or unit-plateau assumption.

Each positive-degree coordinate monomial has zero integral against $K_\Lambda$ when the smooth supported symbol is one on the unit ball. The moment is proportional to the corresponding derivative of the symbol at frequency zero, which vanishes on the plateau. This cancels the positive-degree terms of the Taylor polynomial.
e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_scaledLiftK: The substitution $z=\Lambda y$ cancels the $\Lambda^3$ in the kernel against the Jacobian and leaves $\Lambda^{-k}$ from $|y|^k$. Thus the absolute $k$th moment scales by $\Lambda^{-k}$ for every $\Lambda>0$. The paper uses a Schwartz kernel, so both integrals are finite. Lean also states the identity for arbitrary kernels under its convention that a nonintegrable integral equals zero.

e03-appc-admissible-order.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_steps: Assume $q_1=1$, $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$, nondecreasing frequencies, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$ for $j\ge1$. The formal statement concludes $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$. Its proof first shows $\mathcal B(q_j)\le\lambda_{j-1}$ and $q_j\ge1$, which is the admissibility claimed in the quotation. Those membership conditions are intermediate proof steps, not the declaration's displayed conclusion. No monotonicity of $\mathcal B$ is assumed.

e03-appc-threshold.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_advan: The formal statement proves $q_{j+1}=q_j+1$ exactly when the next threshold is met, assuming the maximum rule. The paper also says that otherwise $q_{j+1}=q_j$. That second assertion requires current-order admissibility, provided by the separate order-step result. The threshold equivalence alone does not state it.
e03-appc-threshold.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_steps: The paper identifies the precise threshold at which the order increases. This result proves only $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$; the separate threshold equivalence determines which of the two possibilities occurs.

e03-appc-frequency-growth.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_frequency_t: The formal statement assumes an integer $b\ge1$, initial frequency $N>1$, and the recurrence $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^{320b(q_{j+1}+1)}$. It proves $\lambda_j\to\infty$ without imposing the threshold selection rule, which is unnecessary for this particular growth conclusion.

e03-appc-order-growth.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_tends: Assuming increasing frequencies tending to infinity, the initial condition and the maximum rule in (1.14), the formal statement proves $q_j\to\infty$. Its proof successively exceeds each finite threshold, exactly as described here. It does not assume monotonicity of the threshold function itself.

e03-appc-three-steps.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_three_log_s: With the formal index $i=j-1$, its identity is $L_{i+2}=4K(q_{i+1})K(q_{i+2})K(q_{i+3})\log\lambda_i$, which is the displayed equation. The formal recurrence uses nonnegative integer powers. The paper's positive frequencies give the ordinary logarithmic interpretation.

e03-r2-appc-exponent-monotonicity.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: The paper bounds three consecutive exponents by $K(q_{j+1}+1)$. The formal declaration concludes the final logarithmic gain bound. The three exponent inequalities are intermediate deductions inside its proof from the two stated order comparisons. It does not expose their conjunction as its conclusion.

e03-appc-floor.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: Let $b\in\mathbb N$, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, $\lambda_{r+1}=\lambda_r^{K(q_{r+1})}$ and $L_r=4\log\lambda_{r+1}$. At $j\ge1$, assume $q_j\le q_{j+1}$, $q_{j+2}\le q_{j+1}+1$, $0<\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\lambda_{j-1}$, and $4K(q_{j+1}+1)^3\le\log\mathcal B(q_{j+1})$. The formal statement proves $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$. It needs only these local conditions, rather than the complete admissibility and maximum-rule assumptions used to obtain them in the paper.
e03-appc-floor.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer and $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. Assume $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$, $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. The formal theorem proves the one-step order bounds, $q_j\to\infty$, and $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$. It omits only the paper's additional threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination. The initial and maximum-rule assumptions remain essential hypotheses.

e03-appc-cubic-floor.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: The paper displays the chain bounding the product of three exponents by the logarithm of the preceding frequency. The formal declaration concludes $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$; its proof contains the displayed product and threshold inequalities. Those intermediate inequalities are not the declaration's stated conclusion.

r5-app-weighted-directions.TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection: The formal object is the family $\ell_*\partial_{a_1},\ell_*\partial_{a_2},\ell_*\partial_{a_3},h\partial_s$. These are exactly the two scales in the quoted sentence; positivity and the particular values selected in Subsection 5.1 are additional context.
r5-app-weighted-directions.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm: The finite derivative sum uses the scaled label and phase directions, giving one factor $\ell_*$ per label derivative and one factor $h$ per phase derivative. The time set and boundedness of the resulting derivative families must also be specified when using it as the paper's norm.

r5-app-fixed-parent-power.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The formal estimate retains one factor $C_{\rm low}$ at every finite order when the weighted coefficient bounds (D.7) hold. It does not assign a power of $\mathsf D$ to $C_{\rm low}$ or prove those coefficient bounds. Those applications are needed to infer the derivative-independent power asserted here.
r5-app-fixed-parent-power.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: For the parent flow of §5.1, set $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Given an integer $C_A\ge0$, the formal assertion chooses one radius threshold before derivative order and proves $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for all $m\ge1$, where $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$. It does not identify $A$ with an inverse bound or assert every mean and transverse estimate. Its parent hypotheses are the standing hypotheses of §5.1: $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, $U$ smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free with frequencies at most $2\mathsf D$, the bounds (5.1), $R_U$ odd with frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and the coercivity (5.2). The pressure may be any smooth periodic pressure whose residual has these properties.

e03-appd-exact-order-norm.TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex: The paper introduces exact-order derivative sums for general fields. The formal expression specializes to phase-independent coefficients in a real normed algebra, with suprema over the chosen time set and $\mathbb R^3$. Boundedness must be established before its real-valued supremum expression measures those derivatives.
e03-appd-exact-order-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.coefficientOr: The formal expression gives the exact-order sum for a phase-independent field in an arbitrary real normed space, counting each multi-index once and taking the supremum in time and label. The paper's notation also covers phase-dependent fields and derivatives in physical position. Smoothness and boundedness are not conclusions of the expression.

e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm: The paper specifies both the mixed finite norm and its amplitude-weighted version. This expression is a general sum of real suprema of specified successive derivatives. The scaled coordinate directions, the chosen time set, and normalization by $\gamma$ must be supplied to obtain (D.1); boundedness is also required for the usual norm interpretation.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection: The paper defines two norms. This formal object supplies only the four directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_1},\ell_*\partial_{a_2},\ell_*\partial_{a_3},h\partial_s$. The sum over mixed orders, the time supremum and division by $\gamma(t)$ occur in separate definitions.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm: The paper defines both norms in (D.1). This expression is the unweighted derivative sum only, with one term for each pair $(\beta,j)$ and suprema over all times, labels and phases. The time set, positive scales, periodicity and boundedness must be specified as in the paper; none is proved by the definition.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField: For positive $\ell_*,h$ and $\gamma(t)>0$ on $I=[t_0,T]$, the formal expression is exactly $\sum_{|\beta|+j\le n}\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup_{t\in I,a\in\mathbb R^3,s\in\mathbb R}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^j(f/\gamma)|$. Each mixed multi-index occurs once. Under smoothness and boundedness of these normalized derivatives it is the weighted norm in (D.1). The definition also permits other time sets and zero weights; at $\gamma(t)=0$ it assigns the normalized field zero. Those extra values lie outside the paper's stated positive-amplitude setting and do not change the formula there.

r5-app-weighted-time-domain.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField: The formal expression allows any time set and scalar function $\gamma$; it does not identify that function with a seed amplitude or require positivity. Choosing the time set $[t_0,T]$ and the positive seed amplitude gives the paper's norm. At a zero value of $\gamma$, the bare expression instead assigns the normalized field zero.
r5-app-weighted-time-domain.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: The formal estimates require a positive time weight on an arbitrary time set, but do not identify it with the amplitude of a particular wave. Taking the set $[t_0,T]$ and the given positive amplitude supplies the stated application. No regularity in time is needed for these purely spatial and phase derivative estimates.

e03-r2-appd-phase-independent-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm_pha: For a spatially smooth phase-independent coefficient and $\ell_*\ge0$, the formal statement identifies its mixed derivative expression with $\sum_{m\le n}\ell_*^m|c|_m$ for every phase weight $h$. Every positive phase derivative is zero. As an identity of expressions it does not establish boundedness.

e03-r2-appd-holder-norm-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderOrderNo: The paper denotes the exact-order half-Hölder quantity without fixing the internal norm convention. This definition uses the maximum of the uniform norm and seminorm; replacing it by their customary sum changes the norm by at most a factor two.
e03-r2-appd-holder-norm-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderFieldNo: The paper gives the weighted Hölder norm without fixing how its uniform and seminorm parts are combined. The formal norm uses their maximum for each derivative, equivalent within a factor two to the customary sum convention.

The paper groups the Hölder norm by derivative order. This identity gives that grouping with the maximum convention for each Hölder contribution; replacing the maximum by the customary sum costs at most a factor two, which the paper’s constants absorb.

e03-r2-appd-holder-interpolation.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o: The formal statement proves $|v(x)-v(y)|\le\sqrt{2AB}\,|x-y|^{1/2}$ for differentiable $v$ with uniform bounds $|v|\le A$ and $\|Dv\|\le B$, $A,B\ge0$. Taking the finite supremum bounds gives the paper's seminorm inequality, including coincident points without division.
e03-r2-appd-holder-interpolation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2: The paper gives the geometric-mean interpolation inequality. This formal declaration states the later finite-norm comparison (D.2), with constant four and bounded-derivative hypotheses. Its proof uses the interpolation inequality, but the declaration itself does not state that inequality as a separate conclusion.

e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis: The paper gives both the exact-order interpolation bound and the summed comparison. This result supplies only the final comparison and already assumes the Hölder quantities are finite. The full statement of (D.2) proves that finiteness and both bounds.
e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2: For $0<\ell_*\le1$ and smooth coefficients with derivatives bounded through the required next order, the formal statement proves both bounds in (D.2) and the necessary Hölder finiteness. Its constant is four under the maximum convention for each Hölder norm. The paper leaves that convention unspecified; choosing the customary sum merely changes the unspecified absolute constant.
e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2: The formal theorem proves all of (D.2) for $0<\ell_*\le1$, using smooth coefficients with bounded next derivatives. Its Hölder norm takes the maximum of supremum and seminorm, and its explicit constant is four. The equivalent sum convention gives the same paper inequalities with an adjusted absolute constant. The lower norm comparison is included.

e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives: Let $\ell_*,h>0$ and let $f(t,a,s)$ be spatially and phase smooth, with bounded mixed derivatives through order $n+1$ over a specified time set, all labels and phases. The formal statement proves $\sum_i\|\partial_{a_i}f\|_{[n]}\le3\ell_*^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$ and $\|\partial_sf\|_{[n]}\le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$, counting each multi-index once. Applying it to $f/\gamma(t)$ gives (D.3) when those normalized derivative families are bounded; positivity alone does not supply that boundedness. The product estimate (D.4) is not a conclusion here.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: Let $B$ be a continuous bilinear map and let $f,g$ be spatially smooth fields. Choose smooth differentiation directions, a time weight $\gamma$, and an order $n$; assume bounded derivative families through order $n$ for $f$ and $g/\gamma$. The formal statement gives $\|B(f,g)/\gamma\|_{[n]}\le2^{n+1}N_n\|B\|\|f\|_{[n]}\|g/\gamma\|_{[n]}$, where $N_n$ counts the nondecreasing derivative sequences through order $n$. With the scaled label and phase directions this yields (D.4). The derivative estimates in (D.3) are separate. This helper also permits zero weights, using zero for division by zero. The paper assumes positivity.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: For $\ell_*,h>0$, a positive time weight $\gamma$ and fields smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, assume uniformly bounded normalized derivatives of $f/\gamma$ through $n+1$ for (D.3), and of $f$ and $g/\gamma$ through $n$ for (D.4). The formal statement gives the displayed derivative inequalities with label constant three and extends the product to every continuous bilinear $B$, multiplying the bound by $\|B\|$. It also establishes boundedness of each output derivative family. The finite norm counts each mixed multi-index once over the chosen time set.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1: For positive scales and a positive time weight, the formal theorem proves (D.3) with label constant three and (D.4) for every continuous bilinear product, including its operator norm. The fields are smooth in label and phase. Required bounds are on $f/\gamma$ through order $n+1$ for differentiation, and on $f$ and $g/\gamma$ through order $n$ for products; they are uniform over the chosen time set, labels and phases. Each multi-index is counted once and the output derivative families are bounded. These hypotheses make the displayed weighted norms ordinary finite norms.

e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage: Let $f:I\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to E$ be smooth in label and phase, period-one in phase, with $E$ a real Banach space. Assume uniformly bounded derivatives through order $n$ along a chosen finite family of constant directions. The formal statement proves contraction of the phase average and the factor-two bound for subtracting it in the corresponding derivative sum. Choosing the scaled coordinate directions and applying it to $f/\gamma(t)$ gives the first two inequalities in (D.5), provided those normalized derivatives are bounded. It contains no primitive estimate.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive: For a real Banach-valued field smooth in label and phase, period-one in phase and of zero phase mean, assume bounded derivatives through order $n$ along a finite family of constant directions, uniformly over all times, labels and phases. The formal statement bounds its zero-mean periodic primitive by twice the input in that derivative sum. Applying it to $f/\gamma(t)$ with the scaled coordinate directions yields the last inequality in (D.5), provided the normalized derivatives are bounded. Averaging and subtraction of the mean are treated separately.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: Phase averaging has norm at most one on the mixed derivative norm, so subtracting the average has norm at most two. The periodic primitive with zero phase mean also has norm at most two on a centered input. The estimates assume finite scaled derivative bounds and positive time weight. The primitive requires the input mean to vanish.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1: For positive scales, a positive time weight and a period-one real Banach-valued field smooth in label and phase, the formal theorem proves the three inequalities in (D.5), with primitive constant two. It assumes uniformly bounded mixed derivatives of $f/\gamma$ through the stated order, and the primitive estimate additionally requires zero phase mean. All output derivative families are bounded. The averaging interval is $[0,1]$; the normalized primitive is the integral from phase zero minus its average. These are the paper's phase operations, with an explicit primitive constant.

e03-appd-holder-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: The paper states the product estimate in the half-Hölder norm without fixing its internal convention. This result uses the maximum of the uniform and Hölder parts. The equivalent sum convention gives the same estimate after adjusting the order-dependent constant.
e03-appd-holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: The paper states a half-Hölder product estimate. The formal statement permits continuous bilinear products and uses the maximum convention with an explicit constant; replacing it by the customary sum changes only the constant.

e03-r2-appd-derivative-count.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1: The paper describes the counting argument that gives the label constant three and the phase shift. The formal declaration states all estimates of Lemma D.1 rather than this counting assertion. Its proof sums three coordinate estimates and applies the phase-direction estimate, producing the same derivative bounds without exposing the quoted combinatorial sentence as a conclusion.

e03-appd-product-proof.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: The quoted sentence describes the product-rule argument. The formal statement gives the resulting finite derivative-norm bound for a general continuous bilinear product and time weight; its proof moves the scalar factor inside that product and invokes the derivative product estimate. The product-rule identity itself is not the declaration's conclusion.
e03-appd-product-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1: The formal declaration proves the complete Lemma D.1. In its product clause it applies the bilinear derivative estimate to $f$ and $g/\gamma$, as the paper describes. The quoted proof instruction is an explanation of that clause, not a mathematical conclusion stated by this declaration.

e03-appd-average-contraction.TorusEuler.norm_phaseMean_le: The formal bound is $|\int_0^1f|\le M$ whenever $|f(s)|\le M$ on $[0,1]$. For the paper's smooth profiles this says exactly that phase averaging has supremum norm at most one. The standalone bound does not require periodicity and does not independently establish integrability of an arbitrary input.

e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.phasePrimitive: For $f:\mathbb R\to E$ in a real normed space, the formula is $F(s)=\int_0^sf(r)\,dr-\int_0^1\int_0^qf(r)\,dr\,dq$. It subtracts the mean of the integral, not its value at phase zero. The definition alone does not assert periodicity, zero mean or recovery of $f$ by differentiation. Those are separate conclusions for the continuous, period-one, zero-mean Banach-valued profiles used by the paper.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.periodic_phasePrimitive: For a continuous period-one function $f:\mathbb R\to E$ with $\int_0^1f=0$, where $E$ is a real normed space, form $F$ by subtracting the mean of $s\mapsto\int_0^sf$. The formal statement proves only $F(s+1)=F(s)$. It has no completeness hypothesis. The paper's Banach targets give the ordinary integral interpretation. Zero mean of $F$ and $F'=f$ are separate results requiring a complete target.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.phaseMean_phasePrimitive: Let $f:\mathbb R\to E$ be continuous with $E$ a real Banach space. For $F(s)=\int_0^sf-\int_0^1\int_0^qf$, the formal statement proves $\int_0^1F(s)\,ds=0$. Neither periodicity nor zero mean of the input is required for this normalization. The paper also asserts that the primitive is periodic and differentiates to $f$; those properties come from separate declarations, with zero input mean required for periodicity.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.hasDerivAt_phasePrimitive: Let $f:\mathbb R\to E$ be continuous with values in a real Banach space, and subtract the average from its integral based at phase zero. The formal statement proves $F'(s)=f(s)$ at every real phase. It does not require periodicity or zero input mean, and does not state periodicity or zero mean of the output. The other linked results supply those properties in the paper's period-one, zero-mean setting.

e03-appd-primitive-sup.TorusEuler.norm_phasePrimitive_le: For a continuous one-periodic profile with zero mean and $|f|\le M$ on one period, the formal statement proves that the normalized primitive has size at most $2M$ at every real phase. This is the paper's stated supremum estimate. The bound relies on periodicity and zero mean, not merely on the primitive's formula.

e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.FiniteCoefficientMultiIndexPo: The paper's coefficient convention uses fixed-order constants and an absolute real exponent. This condition chooses its constants after the coefficient and parent parameter are fixed and takes a nonnegative integer exponent. It expresses polynomial control for one coefficient, but not uniform constants for a family; enlarging the exponent also changes the literal powers.
e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.finiteCoefficientPower_iff_mu: The paper displays a coefficient bound. This theorem proves equivalence between coordinate-derivative and operator-norm versions of such bounds. It does not itself establish the bound for the coefficients in the construction.
e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.CoefficientPo: The paper writes an absolute real exponent in (D.6). The formal condition takes the constants as explicit inputs and uses a nonnegative integer exponent; rounding a real exponent upward preserves polynomial control for $\mathsf D\ge1$.

r5-app-coefficient-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.CoefficientPo: The formal condition specifies smoothness and bounded coordinate derivatives for a coefficient $c(t,a)$, with given constants $C_m$ and a nonnegative integer exponent. The paper uses matrix fields and a real absolute exponent. The missing phase variable makes phase independence explicit; no time differentiability is imposed.
r5-app-coefficient-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The formal statement takes separate given constant sequences and integer exponents for the inputs, and chooses uniform output constants before the time domain, parent parameter and fields. Products may be bilinear maps between real normed spaces and inverses lie in complete real normed algebras. These are precise extensions and restrictions of the paper's matrix-field hypotheses.

e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex: The paper uses fixed-order constants to control products in (D.6). This result gives such constants after fixing the parent parameter and coefficients, with integer exponents. The separate full coefficient lemma makes their uniformity explicit.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul: The paper’s coefficient estimates use fixed-order constants. This result proves product closure for fixed coefficients and parent parameter using an integer exponent, so it alone does not express constants uniform over those choices.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The formal statement generalizes the matrix product to any bilinear map of norm at most one and selects output constants uniformly before the parent parameter and fields. However, its input and output exponents are nonnegative integers, with output exponent $2\max(q,r)$. The paper allows real absolute exponents; they can be enlarged for closure, but the scopes do not coincide literally.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: The formal theorem proves uniform product closure for bounded bilinear actions, with exponent $2\max(q,r)$ for integer input exponents. The paper speaks of matrix products with real absolute exponents. Rounding preserves the existence of some polynomial bound for $\mathsf D\ge1$, while the broader target class and restricted exponent parameters make the literal statements different.

e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd: The paper uses fixed-order constants for the inverse coefficient. This result chooses such constants after fixing the parent parameter and coefficient and uses integer exponents. The full coefficient lemma separately states their uniformity.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse: The paper’s inverse estimate uses fixed-order constants. This result proves polynomial control for a fixed invertible coefficient and parent parameter with integer exponents, without itself stating uniform constants across those choices.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The formal statement permits any complete real normed algebra and chooses constants uniformly before the fields and parent parameter. It assumes pointwise invertibility and an inverse bound $\mathsf D^e$, with integer exponents $q,e$, and gives exponent $3\max(q,e)$. The paper uses matrices and real absolute exponents, which may be enlarged when only polynomial closure is required.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: The formal theorem extends inversion from matrices to complete real normed algebras, but states its bounds with nonnegative integer exponents and explicit pointwise invertibility. Uniform output constants are retained. Real exponents in the paper may be rounded for this closure assertion. The linked theorem does not retain them as literal parameters.

e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn: The paper uses the fixed real exponent $C$ in both the scale condition and conclusion. This result permits zero radius but uses an integer exponent and chooses constants after the parent parameter and coefficient; rounding $C$ upward can require a smaller radius.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted: The paper retains its fixed real exponent in part (c). This result allows zero radius and uses an integer exponent, with constants chosen after the parent parameter and field; replacing $C$ by its ceiling changes both the radius requirement and the displayed powers.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The paper assumes $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$ for its fixed real exponent. The formal statement uses an integer exponent $a$ with uniform constants, so rounding $C$ upward changes the condition to $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-\lceil C\rceil}$ and enlarges the powers in the conclusion.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: The paper’s part (c) keeps the real exponent from (D.6). The formal theorem proves the same pattern for integer exponents; upward rounding is adequate when the radius can be chosen smaller, but it changes the literal fixed-exponent statement.

e03-r2-appd-product-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: The paper writes the intermediate power $\mathsf D^{C(m+2)}$ and then enlarges it to exponent $2C$. The formal declaration states the final uniform product bound with integer exponents, using $2\max(q,r)$ for unequal input exponents. Its proof derives the analogous intermediate estimate, but the quoted real-exponent formula is not its declared conclusion.

e03-r2-appd-inverse-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: The paper derives an explicit multi-index recurrence by differentiating $cc^{-1}=I$. The formal proof applies a general higher-derivative estimate for inversion and converts its derivative norms, obtaining the coefficient bound through a different intermediate calculation.

e03-r2-appd-radius-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: The paper factors the weights using the exponent $C$ from (D.6). The formal proof uses the same argument for a nonnegative integer exponent; a real exponent must first be enlarged, with the associated change in the radius condition.

e03-appd-positive-coefficient.TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati: The formal identity distributes each specified sequence of derivatives between coefficients and the unknown. Every correction term differentiates a coefficient at least once, so fewer derivatives remain on the unknown. This is the mechanism described in the paper. The identity assumes commutation with the principal operator and the product rule for coefficient actions.

e03-appd-lifting-equation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The paper writes a differential equation for fields. The formal estimate takes the same finite coefficient-action form in arbitrary real vector spaces with seminorms and specified derivative maps. The equation is an input hypothesis; identifying those spaces with constrained fields and choosing their norms is required before it becomes the paper's equation.
e03-appd-lifting-equation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The formal statement assumes an equation of the displayed algebraic form, with each coefficient action represented by a bilinear map between seminormed spaces. It does not by itself choose spatial or phase-dependent fields. The paper's differential equation is an application obtained after specifying those spaces, derivatives and any prescribed data.

e03-appd-lifting-commutation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The paper assumes derivative commutation for the principal and coefficient operators. The formal hypotheses specify the principal commutation identity and the full product rule for each bilinear coefficient action, with commuting forcing derivatives. They encode the needed calculus rather than asserting commutation for already chosen spatial operators.
e03-appd-lifting-commutation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The formal statement requires the principal commutation identity, the product rule for coefficient actions, and commutation of derivatives on coefficients and forcings. The paper's spatial and phase operators give one such choice, but these identities are hypotheses in an abstract family of linear maps, not conclusions about particular field operators.

e03-r2-appd-constraint-subspace.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The paper describes preserved constraints, prescribed data and equations modulo gradients. The formal statement works with general seminormed solution and forcing spaces, so those conditions must be built into the chosen spaces and differentiation rules before applying the estimate.

e03-appd-low-order.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The formal hypothesis is a zero-order estimate for every admissible unknown with its own forcing $\mathcal Lu$, not just the particular solution ultimately estimated. This is the uniformity needed to apply the estimate to successive derivatives, as the paper's preceding sentence requires.
e03-appd-low-order.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The formal statement assumes $C_{\rm low}\ge0$ and the displayed zero-order estimate for every unknown in the chosen solution space, using the forcing obtained by applying the equation. The forcing space must include the prescribed data. This matches the estimate needed for every differentiated solution, rather than assuming it only for one fixed pair.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-operator-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The paper defines $b_\nu$ as an operator norm. The formal statement permits any nonnegative bound for the corresponding bilinear coefficient action, so the least possible operator bound need not be identified.

e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_: The paper assumes the full exact-order sum bound (D.7). The formal statement derives the corresponding bound for any one derivative composition from that sum, assuming nonnegative operator bounds and commuting coefficient derivatives. It supplies an implication from (D.7), not (D.7) itself.
e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The paper assumes (D.7) for the complete derivative sum at every positive order. This result uses bounds for each individual derivative only through order $n$; the separate comparison of a term with its sum supplies the needed implication.
e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: To prove an estimate at order $n$, the formal statement assumes the exact-order sum bound only for $1\le m\le n$. The paper assumes it for every positive order. Under the specified seminorm and weighted-derivative interpretation, the finite set of hypotheses is strictly sufficient for the same order-$n$ conclusion.

e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The formal estimate has the same single factor $C_{\rm low}$, but is expressed using seminorms and a finite family of derivative maps. Its constant explicitly depends on the number of increasing derivative sequences and on bounds for each coefficient derivative composition. Applying it to (D.1) requires the weighted coordinate directions and the conversion from (D.7).
e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The paper lifts the inverse bound in its label and phase norms. The formal statement permits arbitrary finite families of derivatives and seminormed spaces, needing coefficient bounds only through order $n$, while retaining one factor $C_{\rm low}$.
e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3: The paper gives the estimate in its finite label and phase norms. The formal theorem proves it for a general finite family of derivatives and seminorms, using coefficient bounds only through the requested order and retaining a single zero-order inverse factor.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: For an estimate at order $n$, the formal statement selects $C_n$ after $n$, the numbers $C_m$ and the finite ordered index set for differentiation, but before the spaces, seminorms, derivative maps, coefficients and solution. Thus the constant can depend on the number of available derivative directions, not on the values of their maps. Fixing the paper's three label directions, or those three plus phase, removes this additional general parameter. The asserted dependence is then the one in the quotation.
e03-r2-appd-lifting-constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: The paper records dependence on the order and coefficient bounds. The formal proof’s explicit constant also counts the available derivative directions; these are fixed in the paper’s spatial or space-and-phase applications.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-holder-case.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The paper explicitly states the half-Hölder version. The formal theorem is general in the seminorms, so the Hölder conclusion requires choosing those norms and checking the coefficient and commutation assumptions in that setting.

e03-appd-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati: The paper groups coefficient differentiations by multi-index and binomial coefficient. The formal identity keeps each splitting of a specified derivative sequence separately, requiring the principal commutation and product-rule identities. When coordinate derivatives commute, equal splittings combine to give the displayed multiplicities. The grouped formula is not the declaration's literal form.
e03-appd-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: The paper displays the differentiated equation itself. This proof obtains the lifting estimate by applying the general differentiated-equation argument and converting the coefficient bounds; a separate result states the underlying identity.

e03-appd-weights.TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_: The paper multiplies the differentiated equation by the scale factors and sums it. The formal identity only shows that putting nonnegative weights into the derivative maps multiplies each derivative seminorm by the product of those weights. It accounts for $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j$ but neither assumes the equation nor states the resulting estimate.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-recursion.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The paper groups the recurrence by the number of derivatives falling on a coefficient. The formal proof instead inducts on individual successive differentiations and sums their splittings, yielding the same lower-order mechanism in a different form.

e03-appd-induction.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The paper concludes the finite-norm estimate by induction on derivative order. The formal declaration states an explicit bound for existing solutions in abstract seminormed spaces; its proof performs the derivative induction and sums the estimates. Thus the link supports the proof method, while its stated conclusion is the quantitative inequality.
e03-appd-induction.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: The declaration states the full abstract version of Lemma D.3. Its proof converts the exact-order coefficient bounds into individual derivative bounds and applies the derivative induction. The quoted sentence describes this proof step, not a separate mathematical assertion made by the declaration.

c8-coefficient-radius-gain.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The formal statement gives the retained factor $\ell_*$ when $m\ge1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$, with integer $q$: $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m^{\prime}\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$. The paper invokes D.2(c) with its fixed real exponent. Choosing a larger integer exponent may require a smaller radius.

c8-holder-radius-gain.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of: Assuming the formal statements labelled Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and (D.2), this formal implication treats $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, with $F=D_aX$ and $M=(D_xU)\circ X$ on $[0,T]$. For an integer $C_A\ge0$ it chooses one sufficiently large integer radius exponent, then proves $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for every $m\ge1$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$. The positive scalar $A$ is not identified with an inverse norm here. The parent hypotheses are imported from an omitted definition. This is a conditional mean-coefficient application of the general argument in the quotation.

c8-common-envelope-exponent.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: For each nonnegative integer $C_A$, the formal assertion selects a radius-exponent threshold before the parent, the positive scalar $A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$ and the derivative order. For every larger integer exponent in $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, it gives finite norms and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m/A$ for all $m\ge1$, where $K=(D_aX)^TD_aX$ and $\Omega=(D_aX)^T(M^T-M)D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$. It covers the two mean coefficients only; neither identification of $A$ with an inverse bound nor the transverse application is included. The exact imported parent hypotheses cannot be checked because their defining file is omitted.

c8-auxiliary-abstract-extension.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The paper asserts that a singular solution can be chosen with a smooth velocity extension near the terminal slice of the punctured torus. The formal theorem supplies such a selected solution and a periodic extension on all real times away from $\mathbb Z^3$. It imposes Euler only before the singular time. The larger extension domain is a regularity conclusion.

e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The formal theorem chooses one exponent parameter and one nondecreasing threshold before the initial frequency. Every sufficiently large initial frequency then admits a selected construction with the auxiliary estimates and smooth terminal extension. This establishes the existence of the choice asserted in the paper.
e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: This formal condition describes one threshold, fixed before the initial frequency, for which selected constructions have the auxiliary estimates and terminal extension. It states the required existence assertion. The separate linked theorem proves it.
e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: This formal assertion asks for the choice for every permitted cutoff and every threshold satisfying two prescribed majorants, after its exponents and majorants are chosen, so as a statement it is stronger than the paper's sentence. The authors' formalization records it as not proved, keeps it outside the chain of proofs of the main theorems and does not use it. The stronger label describes the statement only; what the paper asserts is established by the separately proved selected-construction theorem.

e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: For the selected singular solution, the formal theorem supplies a spatially periodic velocity extension smooth on $\mathbb R\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The paper requires it only near the terminal slice of the punctured torus. Agreement is required on the full preterminal punctured slab, and no Euler equation is imposed after the singular time.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.HasSmoothOffOriginExtension: This extension condition uses all real times off the integer lattice, rather than only an open neighborhood of the terminal slice. The field is periodic and equals the original velocity for $0\le t<T$. It defines the required extension property. It is not itself a proof that a given velocity has it.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: The extension clause is the paper's, but the complete formal assertion demands it for every qualifying cutoff and threshold after its exponents and majorants are chosen, which makes the statement stronger than the sentence. The authors' formalization records this generalized assertion as not proved and unused by the main theorems. The extension the paper needs is supplied by the proved selected-construction theorem, not by this statement.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension: The formal condition is a periodic lift of precisely this extension: one field is jointly smooth on an open neighborhood of $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and on the preterminal punctured slab, and agrees there with $u$. It does not impose a pressure or Euler equation beyond $T$.

e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The formal theorem retains the main listed singularity conclusions for the same selected solution, including maximality, bounded velocity, divergent time integrals, central vorticity blow-up and spatial limits off the origin. It does not itself compare that solution with every other maximal solution from the same initial data. The proved Remark 1.2 adds that uniqueness comparison.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: This condition includes all listed singularity properties for the same velocity and terminal time, but contains no comparison with another maximal solution from the same datum. The complete formal version of the main result includes that uniqueness comparison, which is supplied in the proved Remark 1.2.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: The stated conclusions keep the main singularity properties and uniqueness, but the formal assertion quantifies over every qualifying cutoff and threshold, which makes it stronger as a statement. The authors' formalization records it as not proved and unused by the main theorems. The retained conclusions are established by the proved selected-construction theorem together with the proved Remark 1.2.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2: The proved version of Remark 1.2 combines the selected singular solution and its smooth extension with periodic Euler uniqueness. It retains all main conclusions and shows that any other maximal solution of finite real lifespan with the same initial velocity has the same terminal time and agrees on the entire preterminal interval.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2: This proved statement of Remark 1.2 asserts existence of a solution with the main singularity conclusions, the comparison with every maximal solution of finite real lifespan from the same data, and smooth terminal velocity extension away from the torus origin. It is the completed existence formulation needed here.

e03-aux-equation-domain.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution: The formal Euler equations are required for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and $0\le t<T$. At $t=0$ the time derivative is taken from within this interval. Smoothness and periodicity of velocity and pressure, and zero spatial mean of pressure, are also required there. No equation at or beyond $T$ is imposed.
e03-aux-equation-domain.TorusEuler.HasSmoothOffOriginExtension: This condition only asks for a smooth periodic velocity extension agreeing with $u$ on $[0,T)$ away from the lattice. It imposes no Euler equation anywhere. The separate Euler-solution condition is what supplies the equation on the preterminal interval.

e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step: The paper chooses a threshold that bounds the actual time-derivative constants. This formal construction only enlarges a supplied list of constants by sums of their absolute values over time and spatial orders, with an extra spatial reserve. It does not prove that these entries bound the analytic estimates or by itself select the threshold.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_: For finite constant families, the formal statement bounds each additional constant by the threshold built from the enlarged list. It allows time order and depth up to $7K(s)$ and spatial order up to $7K(s)+r(q,P)$, with an arbitrary nonnegative reserve. The paper names the unreserved range; setting the reserve to zero gives it.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeDerivativeThres: The formal condition is only $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ for every $s\ge1$. It does not prove that $G$ bounds any analytic constants, nor does it itself impose monotonicity or the main lower bound on $\mathcal B$. Those are separate parts of the construction.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol: Given majorants $F$ and $G$, this result constructs a threshold satisfying the main admissibility inequalities and $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$. It proves numerical compatibility of the two threshold requirements, not the analytic assertions that the chosen majorants bound the constants in the estimates.

e03-aux-threshold-before-frequency.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis: The formal result fixes the enlarged threshold from the prescribed constant families before finding an initial-frequency lower bound. For every larger initial frequency it then supplies a schedule with that same threshold, the specified initial frequency, the main numerical bounds and the additional constant bounds. The fields are constructed separately from this numerical schedule.

e03-r2-aux-threshold-growth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters: The formal schedule includes $\mathcal B(q_{i+2})\le\lambda_i$ among the requirements determining the next spatial order. With $j=i+1$, this is the displayed inequality for $j\ge1$. The linked declaration states this requirement. Existence of a schedule satisfying it is proved separately.

e03-aux-same-fields.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: One selected construction supplies all the velocity, residual and oscillation fields occurring in the time bounds and mixed correction bounds. Thus the extra estimates concern that construction's own $U_j$, as the paper says. The same formal condition also asks for a singular solution and smooth extension with the same terminal time, but does not explicitly require convergence of those stages to that solution. The supplied assembly proof does construct and use the actual stage limit. The absence is in the exported condition, not a demonstrated failure of the construction.

e03-aux-slabs-beyond-terminal.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The formal condition supplies $T>0$ as the limit of the activation times, requires $T<S_j$ for every stage, and uses this same $T$ as the maximal time in the singularity conclusions. The stage fields are smooth on their closed intervals. Thus the auxiliary construction retains $S_j>T_\infty=T_*$.
