e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12: The formal theorem chooses a selected construction in which every fixed pair $(m,q)$ has a starting stage after which the mixed correction bound and its time-continuity clause hold. The starting stage is allowed to depend on both derivative orders and the construction.
e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi: The formal condition has exactly the order of quantifiers stated here: for each fixed pair of nonnegative integers $(m,q)$, the bound holds at all sufficiently large stages. It records that eventual property for a given sequence. It does not itself assert time continuity or prove the condition.
e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2: The paper states eventual bounds for its selected construction. This formal assertion instead ranges over every construction satisfying the specified threshold and Section 7 step data, with a majorant chosen before the construction, so as a statement it is stronger. The authors' formalization records it as not proved and unused by the main theorems. The eventual bounds for the selected construction are proved separately.

e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12: The proved selected-construction theorem gives the eventual bound and continuity in the formal spatial Hölder norm on each closed child interval. The accompanying vocabulary identifies this with the stated time-space norm and describes full spatial derivatives. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se: This result supplies continuity of the selected correction in the spatial Hölder norm on $[0,S_j]$ after every fixed time derivative. It does not give the bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$ or choose the eventual starting stage required by the displayed estimate.
e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.MixedIncrementBound: This condition states the fixed-stage inequality together with continuity in time in the spatial Hölder norm, using derivatives at fixed physical position within $[0,S_j]$. It does not assert eventual validity. The norm is described in the supplied vocabulary, but its defining formula is imported from an omitted file.

e03-aux-fixed-spatial-point.TorusEuler.slabTimeJet: The formal derivative fixes $x$ and differentiates $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ within the closed stage interval. For a smooth field on a positive interval these are the classical derivatives in its interior and the one-sided endpoint derivatives. The definition alone makes no smoothness assertion.

e03-aux-mixed-starting-index.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi: The formal condition places the choice of a sufficiently late stage after the fixed integers $m,q$. It therefore permits that stage to depend on both orders and imposes no single starting index that works simultaneously for all derivative orders.

e03-r2-aux-time-step-order.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal: The paper explains why the actual residual construction closes the time-order induction. The linked condition merely asks that parent velocity-residual bounds through order $q$ imply the child bounds and mixed correction estimate through order $q+1$, eventually. It neither proves these implications nor states the formula showing how the child's residual uses the parent's residual.

e03-aux-time-quantifiers.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13: For each fixed time order and selected construction, the formal theorem supplies one nonnegative integer exponent and one eventual starting stage, uniform over $i\le q$. The paper allows an unspecified exponent. This more specific choice is harmless because $\lambda_j\ge1$, so increasing a real exponent to a nonnegative integer preserves an upper bound.
e03-aux-time-quantifiers.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3: The formal assertion asks for such exponents and stages for every construction with the prescribed threshold and step data, whereas the paper concerns the selected construction, so as a statement it is stronger. The authors' formalization records it as not proved and unused by the main theorems. The bounds for the selected construction are proved separately, with an integer exponent and one starting stage for each time order.

e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13: The selected-construction theorem supplies both inequalities for every $i\le q$ at all sufficiently large stages, together with continuity of the time curves in the spatial supremum norm. These are periodic continuous fields, so their spatial supremum gives the intended $L^\infty$ bound.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim: This result only turns assumed pointwise stage bounds into the two spatial supremum inequalities at a specified time and order. It does not choose the exponent or eventual stage and does not assert continuity of the time curves in that norm.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim: This condition records the two pointwise inequalities through order $q$ at one fixed stage. It omits time continuity and the choices of an exponent and an eventual starting stage. Those additional assertions occur in the full auxiliary lemma.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeBounds: This fixed-stage condition includes both pointwise inequalities and continuity of both time curves in the spatial supremum norm on $[0,S_j]$. Its exponent is a nonnegative integer. The auxiliary lemma adds the existential choice of that exponent and eventual validity.

e03-aux-time-frequency-support.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve: The paper states Fourier support bounds for both fields. This result gives only the velocity support, at most $2\lambda_j^5$, for every nonnegative time order on the closed positive stage interval. It represents the derivative as a continuous torus field. The residual bound requires the paired result.
e03-aux-time-frequency-support.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re: This result gives only the residual support, at most $4\lambda_j^5$, for every time order on the closed positive stage interval, assuming $\lambda_j\ge0$. The velocity support in the same paper sentence is a separate conclusion.

e03-aux-bernstein-cost.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl: The formal result chooses $C_m$ before the stage and time order and gives the cost $C_m\lambda_j^{5m}$ for a full spatial derivative of either time-differentiated field. The paper uses coordinate partial derivatives; their finite sum is controlled after an order-dependent change in $C_m$. The constant remains independent of the time order.

e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal: The result performs the time-order induction for a fixed sequence once both analytic step implications are assumed, with frequencies at least one and spatial orders tending to infinity. It produces the eventual pointwise time and mixed correction bounds, but does not prove the analytic implications or time-continuity clauses.
e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co: This proved implication derives the generalized form of Lemma 1.3, for every qualifying construction, from a uniform time-step hypothesis. The authors' formalization records that hypothesis as an open input and the generalized lemma as not proved and unused by the main theorems. The induction the paper describes is carried out for the selected construction inside the proved selected-construction theorem.
e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co: This proved implication derives the generalized form of Lemma 1.2 from the main order-growth lemma, the generalized Lemma 1.3 and a uniform correction-step hypothesis. The authors' formalization records the step hypothesis as an open input and both generalized lemmas as not proved and unused by the main theorems. For the selected construction the corresponding estimate is proved inside the selected-construction theorem.

e03-aux-base-mixed.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix: When $m\le q_j$, this result gives the finite spatial Hölder measurement and its bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$ throughout the child interval. This is the numerical base estimate at time order zero. The full auxiliary Lemma 1.2 also includes continuity in that norm, which this declaration does not state.

e03-aux-base-time.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim: Assuming all frequencies are at least one, the formal result gives $|U_j|\le\lambda_j$ and $|R_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ at every stage, hence the pointwise estimates with $\psi_0=1$. The paper's time-space norm also requires continuity in the spatial supremum norm. That comes from a separate result.

e03-aux-parent-polynomial-slab.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term: The paper treats $T^{-1}$, $\ell_*^{-1}$ and fixed powers of $\mathsf D$ as parent-frequency powers. Under $\lambda_0\ge e$ and nonnegative activation time, this result proves only $T^{-1}\le\mu^{1/8}$. It contains no bound for the label radius and no assertion about the other powers.

e03-aux-parent-projected-equation.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ: For time order $r+1$, the formal identity is $\partial_t^{r+1}U=\partial_t^rR_U-\mathbb P\sum_{i=0}^r\binom ri((\partial_t^iU)\cdot\nabla)\partial_t^{r-i}U$. Taking $r=q-1$ gives the paper's positive-order formula. The stage is incompressible, so the advection sum is the tensor-divergence expression. The identity holds on the closed stage interval.

e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te: The formal result has the same derivative powers and one-order difference between velocity and residual, after shifting its time index by one. However, it chooses the common spatial constants only after the time order and input velocity exponent. Its residual constant may therefore depend on those data, whereas the paper displays $C_n$ independently of the time order. The separate Bernstein result has the sharper uniformity.
e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: For the selected parent on the child interval, this result gives the same powers $\mu^{5n}$ and $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and uses one fewer residual time derivative. Its common spatial constants are chosen after the time order and input exponent, so it does not retain the displayed residual constant's independence from those parameters.
e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl: The formal Bernstein theorem fixes its spatial constants before every time order and stage. It therefore supplies the uniform $C_n\Lambda_U^n$ conversion for the residual, once its pointwise time bounds are known. It does not itself prove the parent velocity time bounds or the whole pair of estimates in (2.1).

e03-aux-no-high-residual-jet.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The formal result assumes parent velocity and residual bounds through order $r$ and concludes velocity bounds through order $r+1$, but residual bounds only through order $r$. Taking $r=q-1$ gives the derivative count in the paper: no residual derivative of order $q$ is used in this parent step.

e03-aux-residual-coefficient-jets.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The paper gives a finite label-norm bound for $R_U\circ X$ with a parent exponent independent of label order. This result gives its raw mixed derivative bounds, retaining $\lambda^{-5/2}$ but with spatial factor $(\mu^9)^{16m}$. Applying the label weights and summing is an additional step. The linked conclusion is not itself the displayed finite-norm inequality.

e03-r2-aux-parent-coefficient-bounds.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc: The paper lists the primitive coefficients together with $K$ and $\mathcal D$ in weighted finite norms with an order-independent parent exponent. This formal condition records raw derivatives only of the flow derivative, its inverse, $M$, the normalized covector, its reciprocal squared length and the transported residual. Its raw spatial factor is $\mathsf D^{16m}$; the radius weights and separate product estimates are needed for the paper's statement.

e03-aux-time-norm.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ: For $T>0$, the formal definition is exactly the finite sum $\sum_{i=0}^l T^iN(\partial_t^if)/i!$ for a chosen spatial seminorm $N$. Time differentiation holds label and independent phase fixed. The definition provides the time weighting. The choice and exact normalization of $N$ remain separate.

e03-aux-fixed-label-phase.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD: The formal derivative is the derivative in the time direction $(1,0,0)$ of the profile variables $(t,a,s)$ on $[0,T]$, with $T>0$. It fixes both $a$ and $s$ and uses one-sided derivatives at the time endpoints. It is not the derivative at a fixed physical point.

e03-aux-amplitude-after-derivative.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The formal time sum first applies each time derivative to the profile and then applies the amplitude-weighted spatial seminorm. Hence the positive central amplitude divides the differentiated profile on the active interval. It is not itself differentiated. The exact underlying spatial-seminorm formula is imported from an omitted file.

e03-aux-mean-without-amplitude.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The formal mean measurement is the factorially weighted sum of the unweighted spatial seminorms of its time derivatives on the full selected stage interval. No central-amplitude denominator is introduced. The spatial seminorm is $\|f\|_{[m]}=\sum_{|\alpha|+j\le m}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup_{[0,T],a,s}|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^jf|$, with each multi-index counted once.

e03-aux-extract-time-derivative.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_: For $T>0$ and integers $0\le\ell\le q$, the formal statement proves $N(\partial_t^\ell f)\le\ell!T^{-\ell}\mathcal J_q(f)$ for any chosen spatial seminorm $N$. The nonnegative sum contains its $\ell$th term. Bounding $T^{-\ell}$ by a parent-frequency power is a separate application.

e03-r2-aux-material-graph-identity.TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi:
The paper asserts the material-derivative identity at every nonnegative time order. The linked theorem proves only $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla)f^
atural=(\partial_tf)^
atural$ on a positive closed slab for a smooth periodic parent and its flow. Higher orders follow by applying that identity repeatedly, but are not the stated conclusion of this one declaration.

e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho: For $0\le i\le n$, the formal statement proves $(T^n/n!)\binom ni=(T^i/i!)(T^{n-i}/(n-i)!)$. This is the precise cancellation behind the convolution. It is algebraic and holds for every real $T$; positivity is needed only in the later estimate of norms.
e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le: For positive $T$ and nonnegative sequences, this result bounds the factorially weighted Leibniz sum by the product of the two weighted sums. It is the scalar estimate resulting from the cancellation, not a product theorem for profiles. To obtain the stated profile estimates one must also apply the spatial product inequality.

e03-r2-aux-mean-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe: The formal identity assumes an integrated equation $P(Kv)=c+P\int_0^t(\Omega v+g)$ and differentiates it, with $P$ any bounded linear map. The paper uses the Leray projection and $\mathcal D=2(D_aX)^T\partial_tD_aX$. Recovering its display requires $\Omega=K_t-\mathcal D$, the identity (M.4.2), followed by the binomial rearrangement. The general formal identity does not itself impose those geometric identifications.

e03-r2-aux-mean-time-gain-display.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The scheduled mean estimate controls time order $r+1$ of the mean velocity by time order $r$ of the phase-independent source, with one additional label derivative on the source. Taking $r=q-1$ gives the time-order gain in (2.3). The parent factor is polynomial in $\mathsf D=\mu^9$. The exact normalization of the paper’s imported seminorms is unspecified in this declaration.

e03-aux-mean-gains-time-order.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec: For $q\ge1$, the formal estimate for the selected mean uses source derivatives only through $q-1$, with explicit endpoint-inverse and coefficient bounds on a positive closed slab. It measures the resulting mean through order $q$. At $q=0$, natural-number subtraction makes the source order zero rather than minus one. The inverse and coefficient hypotheses remain necessary.

e03-r2-aux-transverse-time-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The formal result proves this type of time estimate for the selected transverse levels $2\le p\le P$, under the specified parent coefficient bounds and a sufficiently large envelope exponent. It does not assert the estimate for every transverse solution. Its conclusion contains neither the displayed transverse equation nor an independent pressure estimate.

e03-r2-aux-mean-source-order.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The selected measurements use the mean time order $q$ but the mean-source order $\max(q-1,0)$; oscillatory quantities use order $q$. Thus they implement the paper's source-order choice when $q\ge1$. At order zero the source is still measured at order zero. This definition chooses the measurements and does not establish the mean estimate.

e03-r2-aux-residual-time-source-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc: The formal result bounds the transported parent residual in the factorial time norm through order $r$ by a fixed-order constant times $\mathsf D^E\lambda^{-5/2}$, with $\mathsf D=\mu^9$. Taking $r=q-1$ gives this part of the paper's argument. The other source coefficients are controlled at one higher time order. The spatial seminorm is the finite norm (D.1) with label weight $\ell_*$ and phase weight $h$, and the time norm is $\mathcal J_q$.

e03-aux-recurrence-smallness.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even: The formal statement proves eventual $C\mu^A\lambda^{-\varepsilon}\le1$ for every fixed real $C,A$ and every $\varepsilon>0$. Choosing $\varepsilon=1/12$ gives the quoted smallness condition. The starting stage may depend on those fixed quantities, so the theorem does not provide one stage uniform over all derivative orders.

e03-aux-hierarchy-time-lift.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The paper describes estimates for every listed profile, pressure and source. The formal theorem concludes bounds for the aggregate selected oscillation, mean, remainder and activation correction, assuming parent time bounds and explicit smallness. It supplies one parent exponent independent of the admitted spatial order, with order-dependent constants, but does not separately state all component estimates in the quoted paragraph.

e03-r2-aux-aggregate-expansion-rates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc: The formal condition records these aggregate decay factors only for spatial orders satisfying $n+3P\le H$, with supplied constants and parent-loss parameter. It does not assert them at every order in one statement or prove the constants have the paper's allowed dependence. A separate theorem supplies the bounds for the selected expansion as the derivative allowance is enlarged.

e03-r2-aux-oscillatory-spatial-cost.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: The formal result proves $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\lambda^{3/2}\le\lambda^2$ assuming $\lambda>0$ and $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\le\lambda^{1/2}$. This is only the numerical oscillatory factor. It contains no differentiation estimate for a profile and no bound for the phase-independent mean appearing in the same sentence.

c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po: This condition records a bound $\mu^B\lambda^{-5/2}$ for a selected mean's fixed Eulerian time derivative in the formal spatial Hölder norm. It does not prove that bound, assert continuity in time, or give the second inequality $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. The integer exponent and stage are specified inputs.
c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The formal implication absorbs a fixed parent power once the analytic mean and approximation estimates are assumed to follow from the preceding time-order bounds. It then gives the half-size mean estimate eventually at each fixed pair of orders. It does not prove the analytic premises of (2.4).

e03-aux-physical-time-estimates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po: The formal theorem first gives $\mu^B\lambda^{2(n+1)+2q}$ for velocity derivatives and $\mu^B\lambda^{2(q+2)}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ for the residual, under explicit parent, inverse-flow, activation and derivative-reserve hypotheses. The paper's display has already absorbed the parent power into $\psi'_q$. That absorption is a subsequent step, not the conclusion at this link.

e03-r2-aux-tail-depth-identity.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: With $\lambda>0$, $P=6K$ and $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda^K$, the formal identity rewrites $\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$ as $\lambda^{-5/4}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. Cancelling the positive factor $\lambda^{-5/4}$ gives exactly the equality quoted here. The theorem is arithmetic and supplies no analytic estimate for $R_P$.

e03-aux-cutoff-commutation.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: The formal theorem proves $\partial_t^q(S_{\Lambda_j}V)=S_{\Lambda_j}\partial_t^qV$ for the fixed spatial cutoff, with smooth periodic representatives of the time derivatives on the closed slab. Subtracting $\partial_t^qV$ gives the paper's formula for $v_\Lambda$. The linked conclusion itself is the cutoff-velocity identity.

e03-aux-cutoff-tail-estimate.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: For $m\le P$ and $\Lambda>0$, the formal theorem gives $C_P\Lambda^{m-P}\|\partial_t^qV(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$ as a spatial tail bound. It has not substituted $C_P\le\mu$, $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ or the approximate-velocity estimate. Those substitutions produce the paper's displayed expression. Time continuity in the norm is also supplied separately.

e03-aux-half-tail.TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate: The formal result is a single-stage numerical implication: if $\lambda\ge2$, $C\le\lambda$ and $5m+5+\psi'_q\le3P$, then the cutoff expression is at most $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. It does not itself prove that these hypotheses hold at all sufficiently large stages. That uses the schedule and the fact that $m,q$ are fixed.

e03-aux-exact-correction-split.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se: For each selected later step, the formal equality identifies the correction with the actual mean of that step plus its actual Fourier-cutoff error. Its indexing starts with $j=2$. The equality is between the globally defined fields. The auxiliary estimates apply on the closed interval $[0,S_j]$.

e03-aux-add-half-bounds.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Given a smooth split $V=U+O+M$, the explicit depth condition for the cutoff tail and a half-size mean bound, the formal theorem gives $\|\partial_t^q(S_\Lambda V-U-O)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda^{-1}$ at the chosen time. It does not provide the eventual starting stage or continuity in the spatial norm required by the full auxiliary Lemma 1.2.

e03-aux-new-velocity-power.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Let $V$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $T>0$, and use the selected fixed cutoff at $\Lambda=\lambda^5$. At a specified time and order $i$, assume $\lambda\ge2$, $1+C_0\le\lambda$ for the fixed order-zero cutoff constant, and $\|\partial_t^iV\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le\lambda^{2+\psi'_q}$. The formal statement gives $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda^{\psi'_q+3}$ for every $x$. The derivatives are within the closed time interval. Applying the statement at every $i\le q$ and every time gives the quoted supremum bound. The needed approximate-velocity estimates remain hypotheses.

e03-r2-aux-cutoff-residual-identity.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: The formal theorem gives every time derivative of the residual as the Leray projection of the differentiated cutoff residual and a binomial sum of quadratic cutoff errors. At order zero its tensor error is $U_j\otimes U_j-S(V\otimes V)$. With $v=U_j-V$, this equals the three tensors displayed in the paper. The cutoff symbol and scale are fixed in time.

e03-aux-new-residual-power.TorusEuler.slabTimeJet_cutoffResidual_ra: The formal result proves $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ from an assumed analytic residual-error bound and explicit inequalities including $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^K$ and $K\ge16+2\psi'_q$. It is a pointwise implication at a specified order and time. The eventual validity of those assumptions and continuity in the spatial supremum norm are separate parts of the full lemma.

e03-aux-oscillations-leave-compact.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$, the formal theorem gives an open neighborhood of $K$ on which all sufficiently late oscillations vanish for the whole common interval. It applies to any sequence supported in shrinking balls about lattice points, without an Euler equation or mixed derivative hypothesis. The paper's selected oscillations satisfy these support assumptions.

e03-aux-all-jets-terminal-limit.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal: Under the mixed correction bounds, nested stage intervals, square frequency growth and uniform convergence of the velocities on the common closed slab, the formal theorem proves local uniform convergence of every joint space-time derivative to that of the same limit. The neighborhood is a closed cylinder about each point off the integer lattice and includes the terminal time.

Under the same hypotheses, this result concludes only that the given velocity limit is jointly smooth on the closed punctured slab. It does not state uniform convergence of its derivatives. That convergence is the conclusion of the preceding local theorem.

e03-r2-aux-limit-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE: Assume the common stage estimates of Theorem 7.1, an Euler solution with the convergence conclusions of Proposition 8.1, and eventual mixed correction bounds with time continuity at every pair of orders. The linked formal statement concludes a smooth periodic velocity extension through the terminal time away from the lattice. Its proof constructs a smooth closed-slab limit and identifies it with the given $u$ before $T_\infty$, using convergence of the same approximations. That identification occurs inside the proof. It is not a separately stated conclusion of this declaration. No equality of arbitrary assigned terminal values is asserted.

e03-aux-extension-theorem-step.TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio: For a finite-dimensional spatial domain and a Banach-valued field smooth up to the boundary of $[a,T]\times O$, the formal theorem extends it to all later times on the same open spatial set. This gives more domain than the local extension used in the paper. It asserts an extension for each field, not the continuous linear operator in Seeley's original theorem.
e03-aux-extension-theorem-step.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasSmoothOffO: For a preterminal Euler velocity jointly smooth up to the closed punctured slab, the formal theorem gives a periodic extension on all real times off $\mathbb Z^3$, agreeing on the entire physical interval. The paper only needs a neighborhood of the terminal slice. No pressure, incompressibility or Euler equation is asserted for the extension after the singular time.

e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The proved selected-construction theorem supplies a positive limit of the activation times, identifies that time with the maximal time in the singularity conclusions, and gives a smooth periodic velocity extension there off the lattice. This establishes the existence conclusion of the auxiliary note.
e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2: The proved Remark 1.2 adds uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite lifespan from periodic Euler uniqueness to the selected construction's singularity and smooth-extension conclusions. It completes the main paper's strengthened existence assertion without requiring the unproved generalized auxiliary lemma.
e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Proof.theorem_1_1_o: This proved implication assumes Theorem 7.1, the Section 8 results and the generalized mixed-increment lemma for every qualifying construction. The authors' formalization records that lemma as not proved and records this implication as conditional and unused. It therefore gives no unconditional proof of the auxiliary theorem. The conclusion of the sentence is established by the proved selected-construction theorem and the proved Remark 1.2.
